definition_zh: 面对；正视；对抗；使面对面（对质）
definition_en: to bring a person or thing face to face with someone, a fact, or a difficulty
core_image: 两个人被推到同一张桌前，额头对着额头，身后已没有退路
scene: 走廊尽头，两个人迎面站定，谁也不肯先让开。The two rivals confront each other at the end of the corridor.
sceneCN: 这里指两人正面相对、摆出对峙的架势（第 1 个义项：与某人正面相对并形成对峙）；句意：两个对手在走廊尽头正面相对。

derivatives.zh: 令人不得不直面的；使人不安的

senses.title: To stand face to face in hostility
senses.definition: to bring oneself face to face with a person in a tense or hostile way
senses.definitionCN: 在紧张或敌对的状态下与某人正面相对
senses.example: The two neighbours confront each other over the fence every summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个邻居每年夏天都隔着一道篱笆正面相对。
senses.why: The Latin word for forehead is inside the verb, so the picture is two people brow to brow.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词里藏着表示前额的拉丁词，画面就是两个人额头对着额头。

senses.title: To face a problem directly
senses.definition: to deal with a difficulty openly instead of avoiding it
senses.definitionCN: 公开处理困难，而不是回避它
senses.example: The company must confront its falling sales before the year ends.
senses.exampleCN: 公司在年底之前必须正视销售下滑的问题。
senses.why: A problem is imagined as an opponent, so dealing with it borrows the posture of facing a person.
senses.whyCN: 问题被想象成一个对手，因此处理问题借用了面对一个人的姿态。

senses.title: To challenge someone openly
senses.definition: to challenge a person to their face about something they have done
senses.definitionCN: 当面对某人就其所做的事提出质问
senses.example: She confronted her colleague about the missing report.
senses.exampleCN: 她当面质问同事那份不见了的报告。
senses.why: Once two people are face to face, the next step is to speak the charge aloud.
senses.whyCN: 两个人一旦面对面，下一步自然就是把指责说出口。

senses.title: To bring a witness face to face with the accused
senses.definition: in law, to place a witness and an accused person together so that an identification or a story can be tested
senses.definitionCN: 在法律程序中让证人与被告同处一处，以检验辨认或陈述是否可靠
senses.example: The judge allowed the police to confront the witness with the suspect.
senses.exampleCN: 法官准许警方让证人与嫌疑人当面对质。
senses.why: Courts need the physical meeting itself, and the verb names that arrangement.
senses.whyCN: 法庭需要的正是这次当面的会合，这个动词就指这种安排。

senses.title: To place two records side by side
senses.definition: to set two accounts or sets of evidence together so that differences show
senses.definitionCN: 把两份陈述或两组证据摆在一起，使差异显现
senses.example: The historian confronts the letters with the official records.
senses.exampleCN: 这位历史学者把私人信件与官方记录并置对照。
senses.why: Two documents placed face to face are being compared, so the same verb serves comparison.
senses.whyCN: 两份文件被摆成面对面，就是在作比较，同一个动词便兼指对照。

senses.title: To be placed before something (passive)
senses.definition: to find oneself suddenly facing a situation or a mass of material one did not choose
senses.definitionCN: 突然发现自己面对某种并非自己选择的处境或大量材料
senses.example: Visitors are confronted with a wall of rules at the entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 参观者一进门口就被一整面规则挡住。
senses.why: The passive turns the verb around: the person no longer acts but is placed before the thing.
senses.whyCN: 被动语态把动作翻了过来：人不再主动面对，而是被摆到某物面前。

senses.title: To face one's fear or mortality
senses.definition: to look at something frightening or final without turning away
senses.definitionCN: 不转身逃避地注视令人恐惧或终局性的事物
senses.example: The patient chose to confront the diagnosis rather than hide it.
senses.exampleCN: 病人选择直面诊断结果，而不是把它藏起来。
senses.why: The image of standing face to face stretches to whatever cannot be avoided, including death.
senses.whyCN: 正面相对的意象延伸到一切无法回避之事，包括死亡。

senses.title: To oppose a policy or power
senses.definition: to act against a power, policy or tendency that one cannot ignore
senses.definitionCN: 对无法忽视的势力、政策或趋势采取行动加以抵抗
senses.example: Smaller states confront the new tariff at the trade talks.
senses.exampleCN: 较小的国家在贸易谈判中对抗这项新关税。
senses.why: When avoidance is impossible, facing becomes resisting, and the verb takes a collective object.
senses.whyCN: 当回避已不可能，面对就变成抵抗，这个动词也接上集体性的宾语。

intro.en: Confront reached English through French from a medieval Latin verb built on the Latin word for the forehead. The chain of forms is clear, and the original picture is bodily.
intro.cn: 本词经法语来自一个以拉丁语「前额」一词构成的中世纪拉丁动词。各层形式清楚，最初的画面是身体性的。

items.en: Frons, frontis meant the forehead and, by extension, the front of anything; English words for the front and for the brow come from it.
items.cn: 这个拉丁名词指前额，也引申指任何事物的正面；英语中表示前部与前额的词都出自它。

items.en: The prefix com- meant together or with, and it takes a slightly different shape before certain consonants.
items.cn: 这个前缀表示一起、共同，在某些辅音前会换一种写法。

items.en: Medieval Latin built the verb to mean to bring face to face, and used it when parties or witnesses were set before each other.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语造出这个动词，意为使面对面，用于让当事人或证人当面对质。

items.en: Old French carried the verb into legal and military speech, where meeting a person face to face meant standing one's ground.
items.cn: 古法语把这个动词带进司法与军事语境，面对面遇上一个人就意味着站住不退。

items.en: English took the verb in the sixteenth century, first for courtroom confrontation, then for facing problems and hostile powers.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个动词，先用于法庭对质，再扩展到正视问题与对抗势力。

items.en: The passive form fixed the idea of being placed before something one did not choose, which is now its commonest use.
items.cn: 被动形式固定了被置于某事物之前、无从回避的意思，这已成为今天最常见的用法。

note.en: The first group shares the forehead root or its English descendants; the second group names nearby acts of facing and resisting.
note.cn: 第一组共享前额词根或其英语后裔；第二组是相邻的面对与抵抗行为。

entries.definition: The hostile meeting itself, or the act of bringing parties together.
entries.definitionCN: 指敌对的会面本身，或把双方摆到一起的动作。

entries.definition: Of the front or the forehead, as in a frontal attack.
entries.definitionCN: 指正面的或前额的，如正面进攻。

entries.definition: An open insult; it began as a blow to the face and settled on wounded dignity.
entries.definitionCN: 公开的侮辱；原指打脸，后来固定在尊严受损之意。

entries.definition: The face or forward side of anything; the physical part without the hostility.
entries.definitionCN: 任何事物的正面或前部；只有方位，没有敌意。

entries.definition: To stand before something and deal with it; it is the neutral word that needs no hostility.
entries.definitionCN: 站在某物之前并处理它；是无需敌意的中性说法。

entries.definition: To question the rightness of something; the emphasis is on the doubt, not the meeting.
entries.definitionCN: 质疑某事的正当性；强调怀疑，而不是会面。

entries.definition: To meet by chance or in conflict; it stresses the meeting rather than the facing-down.
entries.definitionCN: 偶然或冲突中相遇；强调相遇，而非顶住。

entries.definition: To set about a task or problem with energy; no other person is implied.
entries.definitionCN: 起劲地着手任务或问题；不牵涉另一个人。

entries.definition: To stand against a force; it names the pushing back, while confronting names the standing before.
entries.definitionCN: 顶住一股力量；它指回推，而本词指站到面前。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real forehead root, the real family and fixed phrases that show the argument structure.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的前额词根、真实同族词，以及能显示论元结构的固定搭配。

normal.en: The root is the forehead: two people meet brow to brow.
normal.cn: 词根是前额：两个人额头碰额头地相对。

normal.en: The family runs confrontation, confrontational and confronting.
normal.cn: 同族词有表示对质的、对抗性的与令人不安的三个形式。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: confront a problem, confront the evidence, be confronted with.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：正视问题、直面证据、被置于某物面前。

normal.en: The courtroom sense is the oldest technical one: witness and accused in one room.
normal.cn: 法庭义是最早的技术用法：证人与被告同处一室。

normal.en: The passive turns the verb around: you do not confront, you are confronted.
normal.cn: 被动把动作反过来：不是你去面对，而是你被摆到某物面前。

abstract.en: Picture two rams lowering their heads at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象两只公羊在同一瞬间低下头。

abstract.en: Picture a door that opens only when both people step forward together.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门，只有两人同时向前迈步才会打开。

abstract.en: Picture a mirror that refuses to show anything except the face in front of it.
abstract.cn: 想象一面镜子，除了面前那张脸，什么也不肯照。

examples.en: Teachers confront the same question every term.
examples.cn: 教师们每学期都要面对同一个问题。

examples.en: The report confronts the gap between promise and practice.
examples.cn: 这份报告直面承诺与实践之间的差距。

examples.en: No one wanted to confront the manager about the delay.
examples.cn: 没有人愿意就拖延一事去当面质问经理。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肯」加「撞」——正面撞上，谁也不退，就是面对、对抗

root: 拉丁语「前额、正面」一词加「一起」前缀，构成中世纪拉丁语「使面对面」，再经古法语进入英语；核心画面是额头对额头。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses begin with two people brow to brow and spread to problems, charges, courtrooms, documents, unavoidable situations, death and hostile powers.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从两人额头相对开始，扩展到问题、指控、法庭、文件、无从回避的处境、死亡与敌对的势力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people pushed to one table, brow against brow, with no room left to step back.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人被推到同一张桌前，额头对着额头，身后已没有退路。

branches.en: THE POSTURE: standing face to face in hostility, and the same posture turned toward a problem.
branches.cn: 姿态：敌对地正面相对，以及把同一姿态转向问题。

branches.en: THE CHARGE: the confrontation becomes words spoken to the other person's face.
branches.cn: 当面质问：对峙变成当面对人说出指控。

branches.en: THE COURT: authority places witness and accused in one room.
branches.cn: 法庭：由官方把证人与被告放进同一间屋子。

branches.en: THE COMPARISON: two records held up against each other so that differences show.
branches.cn: 对照：两份记录彼此靠拢，差异随之显现。

branches.en: THE UNAVOIDABLE: a situation one is placed before, a diagnosis one must face, a power one must resist.
branches.cn: 无从回避：被置于面前的处境、必须直面的诊断，以及必须抵抗的势力。

intro.en: Confront is a French and Latin verb whose core is the Latin word for the forehead, with a prefix meaning together.
intro.cn: 本词是经法语而来的拉丁动词，核心是拉丁语中表示前额的名词，外面加一个表示一起的前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies frons and the medieval verb; French supplies the shape that English borrowed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供表示前额的词与那个中世纪动词，法语提供英语实际借入的形式。

items.example: It puts two parties into one meeting.
items.exampleCN: 它把双方放进同一次会面。

items.example: The noun supplies the bodily picture.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供身体性的画面。

items.example: The verb is the legal act of setting parties together.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词指把双方摆到一起的司法行为。

items.example: French carried the verb into courts and camps.
items.exampleCN: 法语把它带进法庭与军营。

items.example: English shortened the borrowed form.
items.exampleCN: 英语把借来的形式缩短定型。

items.example: It builds the noun for the hostile meeting.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示敌对会面的名词。

items.example: It builds the adjective for the manner of such meetings.
items.exampleCN: 它构成描述这类会面方式的形容词。

items.meaning: the activity, or what makes one uneasy
items.meaningCN: 活动本身，或令人不安的性质
items.example: It appears in the participle and in the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在分词与形容词两种用法里。

items.example: The passive frame fixes the unavoidable sense.
items.exampleCN: 被动框架固定了无从回避的含义。

latinEntries.meaning: forehead; the front of a thing

definition_zh: 巩固；使坚实；合并；把……合成一个整体
definition_en: to make something firm and solid, or to press separate parts into one body
core_image: 散落的砖块被压进一块整石，缝隙里灌满灰浆，再也掰不开
scene: 两家小厂把账目、仓库与工人名单并到一处，只留一个管理层。The two firms consolidate their warehouses and accounts into one system.
sceneCN: 这里指把分散的部门与账目合成一个整体（第 2 个义项：把多个单位并入一个机构）；句意：这两家公司把仓库与账目合并成一套系统。

senses.title: To make ground or a structure firm
senses.definition: to press loose material or a built structure until it can carry weight without shifting
senses.definitionCN: 把松散的材料或已建的结构压紧，使其承重而不位移
senses.example: Workers consolidate the soil before the foundation is laid.
senses.exampleCN: 工人在打地基之前先把土层压实。
senses.why: The Latin adjective inside the verb means solid, so the first sense is simply to make something solid.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词里的拉丁形容词意为坚实，因此第一个义项就是使某物变坚实。

senses.title: To merge separate units into one
senses.definition: to combine two or more organizations, departments or functions into a single body
senses.definitionCN: 把两个或更多组织、部门或职能合成一个机构
senses.example: The two firms consolidate their warehouses and accounts into one system.
senses.exampleCN: 这两家公司把仓库与账目合并成一套系统。
senses.why: Units made solid by being joined cannot be pulled apart again, so merging is pictured as hardening.
senses.whyCN: 各单位一旦合成一体便再难拆开，因此合并被想象成变硬的过程。

senses.title: To secure power or control
senses.definition: to make a hold on power or authority firmer and less easy to shake
senses.definitionCN: 使对权力或权威的掌握更牢固、更难动摇
senses.example: The new mayor spent the first year consolidating her support.
senses.exampleCN: 新市长用第一年巩固自己的支持基础。
senses.why: Power that is solid cannot be shaken, so securing it is described as making it solid.
senses.whyCN: 权力若坚实便难以撼动，因此稳固权力就被说成使之坚实。

senses.title: To combine debts or financial claims
senses.definition: to roll several loans or claims into one obligation with a single schedule
senses.definitionCN: 把多笔贷款或债权并成一项义务，只用一张还款表
senses.example: The family consolidated three credit cards into one loan.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人把三张信用卡的欠款并成一笔贷款。
senses.why: Several debts are pressed into one solid block, which is easier to carry and to count.
senses.whyCN: 多笔债务被压成一块整块，既好背负，也好计算。

senses.title: To make learning durable
senses.definition: to repeat and reorganize knowledge until it resists forgetting
senses.definitionCN: 反复复习并重新组织知识，使其不易被遗忘
senses.example: Short daily reviews consolidate what the students learned in class.
senses.exampleCN: 每天短时复习能巩固学生在课堂上学到的东西。
senses.why: A memory becomes solid when repeated practice closes the gaps between its pieces.
senses.whyCN: 反复练习填上记忆碎片之间的缝隙，记忆才变得坚实。

senses.title: To merge scattered records
senses.titleCN: 把分散的记录整合起来
senses.definition: to gather records kept in different places into one store that can be searched as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 把存放在不同地点的记录汇入一个可整体检索的库
senses.example: The hospital consolidated patient files from five clinics.
senses.exampleCN: 这家医院把五个诊所的病人档案整合到一起。
senses.why: Scattered records are like loose bricks; putting them in one store is pressing them into a block.
senses.whyCN: 分散的记录如同散砖，汇入一处就是把它们压成一整块。

senses.title: To lock in a gain or result
senses.definition: to protect a success already won so that it cannot be lost by later change
senses.definitionCN: 保护已经取得的成功，使其不因后续变化而丧失
senses.example: The team consolidated its lead with a second goal.
senses.exampleCN: 球队用第二个进球锁定了领先优势。
senses.why: A win is not safe until it is made firm, so securing a result is called consolidating it.
senses.whyCN: 胜利在变牢之前并不安全，因此保住结果被称为巩固它。

senses.title: Of sediment hardening into rock
senses.definition: in geology, of loose sediment, to harden into rock under pressure and mineral cement
senses.definitionCN: 在地质学中，指松散沉积物在压力与矿物胶结作用下硬结成岩
senses.example: Over millions of years the sand consolidated into sandstone.
senses.exampleCN: 历经数百万年，砂粒固结成了砂岩。
senses.why: Geology kept the most literal sense: loose grains really do become one solid mass.
senses.whyCN: 地质学保留了最字面的含义：松散的颗粒真的会变成一块固体。

intro.en: Consolidate is a Latin verb of solidity: a prefix meaning together and an adjective meaning solid. English took it in the sixteenth century and later stretched it from ground to companies and to memory.
intro.cn: 本词是一个表示坚实的拉丁动词：前缀意为一起，形容词意为坚实。英语在十六世纪借入，后来从土地扩展到公司，再扩展到记忆。

items.en: Solidus meant solid, whole and undivided; the adjective is the part that matters for this verb.
items.cn: 这个拉丁形容词表示坚实的、完整的、不可分的；对这个动词而言，起作用的是形容词义。

items.en: The prefix com- added togetherness and intensity, so the compound meant to make thoroughly solid.
items.cn: 前缀表示一起并加强语气，因此复合词意为彻底使坚实。

items.en: Latin consolidare meant to make firm, and also to knit broken parts into a whole.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词表示使牢固，也指把破碎的部分接合成整体。

items.en: English borrowed it in the sixteenth century, first for making structures, positions and claims firm.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入，先用于使建筑、阵地与主张牢固。

items.en: Banks and companies later used it for pressing many debts or units into one body.
items.cn: 银行与公司后来用它指把多笔债务或多个单位压成一个整体。

items.en: Modern psychology and computing extended it to knowledge and records that must not fall apart.
items.cn: 现代心理学与计算机把它扩展到不可散失的知识与记录。

note.en: The first group shares the solid root or looks close to it; the second group names nearby acts of joining and strengthening.
note.cn: 第一组共享坚实的词根或字形相近；第二组是相邻的连接与加强行为。

entries.definition: The act or result of making firm or of merging units.
entries.definitionCN: 使牢固或合并单位的动作或结果。

entries.definition: Already made firm or already merged, as in consolidated accounts.
entries.definitionCN: 已经变牢或已经合并的，如合并后的账目。

entries.definition: Firm and without gaps; it describes the state the verb produces.
entries.definitionCN: 坚实而无空隙；描述动词造成的结果状态。

entries.definition: To comfort someone in grief; it comes from a different Latin verb and has nothing to do with solidity.
entries.definitionCN: 在悲伤中安慰某人；出自另一个拉丁动词，与坚实无关。

entries.definition: To join two bodies into one; it names the joining without the idea of hardening.
entries.definitionCN: 把两个主体并为一个；只说合并，不含变硬之意。

entries.definition: To make a thing stronger; it may add force without adding solidity.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物更强；可能增添力量而不增添坚实度。

entries.definition: To make parts share one identity; it stresses unity rather than material firmness.
entries.definitionCN: 使各部分共有一个身份；强调统一，而非材质坚实。

entries.definition: To add support to something already there; extra material is brought in.
entries.definitionCN: 在已有之物上加支撑；强调的是外加材料。

entries.definition: To make a hold safe from loss; it names protection rather than compression.
entries.definitionCN: 使所得免于失去；强调保护，而不是压紧。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the solid root, the real family and the fixed phrases of finance and management.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用坚实的词根、真实同族词，以及金融与管理中的固定搭配。

normal.en: Solidus means solid, so the verb begins as a picture of pressing something firm.
normal.cn: 词根意为坚实，动词最初就是把某物压实的画面。

normal.en: The family runs consolidation, consolidated, consolidator and consolidative.
normal.cn: 同族词有表示合并的名词、已合并的形容词、合并者与起巩固作用的形式。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: consolidate power, consolidate gains, consolidate debts.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：巩固权力、锁定成果、合并债务。

normal.en: The business sense is the newest common one: units into one body.
normal.cn: 商业义是较晚普及的用法：把单位并成一个主体。

normal.en: The geological sense is the oldest literal one: loose sand into stone.
normal.cn: 地质义是最字面的用法：松散砂粒变成岩石。

abstract.en: Picture a fist closing on a handful of sand until it holds the shape of the fist.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手握紧一把沙，沙被捏成拳头的形状。

abstract.en: Picture a torn map glued back into one sheet with the seams gone.
abstract.cn: 想象一张撕裂的地图被粘回一整张，接缝消失。

abstract.en: Picture a dozen voices learning to speak one sentence at the same time.
abstract.cn: 想象十几个声音学会在同一时刻说出同一句话。

examples.en: The company consolidated its three regional offices into one headquarters.
examples.cn: 公司把三个地区办事处合并成一个总部。

examples.en: Reviewing the same material twice a week consolidates it in memory.
examples.cn: 每周复习同一材料两次能让它牢牢留在记忆里。

examples.en: The army consolidated its position before the winter set in.
examples.cn: 军队在入冬前巩固了阵地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肯」加「梭里得」——把散沙压成一块整石：巩固、合并

root: 拉丁语「一起、加强」前缀加「坚实」一词，构成「使坚实」，十六世纪进入英语；核心是把松散的压成一块整石。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all press loose things into one firm body: ground, companies, power, debts, memory, records, results and stone.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在把松散之物压成一个坚实整体：土地、公司、权力、债务、记忆、记录、成果与岩石。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: loose bricks pressed into one block, the gaps filled with mortar, impossible to pull apart again.
core.cn: 核心意象：散落的砖块被压进一块整石，缝隙里灌满灰浆，再也掰不开。

branches.en: THE LITERAL: loose ground or a built structure made able to carry weight.
branches.cn: 字面义：松散的土层或建筑被压得能够承重。

branches.en: UNITS JOINED: organizations, warehouses and accounts pressed into one body.
branches.cn: 单位合一：组织、仓库与账目被压成一个主体。

branches.en: POWER AND GAINS: control made unshakable and a lead locked in.
branches.cn: 权力与成果：控制变得不可撼动，领先优势被锁定。

branches.en: THE LEDGER: debts rolled into one loan and scattered records into one store.
branches.cn: 账簿：债务并成一笔贷款，分散记录汇入一处。

branches.en: THE MIND AND THE ROCK: durable memory, and sediment hardened into stone.
branches.cn: 心智与岩石：牢固的记忆，以及固结成岩的沉积物。

intro.en: Consolidate is built from a Latin prefix, a Latin adjective and a verb ending, and its family covers finance, management and geology.
intro.cn: 本词由一个拉丁前缀、一个拉丁形容词与动词词尾构成，其词族横跨金融、管理与地质。

latinIntro.en: Latin solidus and the prefix com- are the two pieces inside consolidare; English added the verb ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示坚实的形容词与表示一起的前缀，是那个拉丁动词内部的两个构件；英语补上了动词词尾。

items.example: It both joins and intensifies the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它既表示结合，也加强那个形容词。

items.example: The adjective supplies the core state.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供核心状态。

items.meaning: to make firm; to knit together
items.example: The verb is the direct ancestor of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是英语词的直接祖形。

items.example: It turns the Latin stem into an English verb.
items.exampleCN: 它把拉丁词干变成英语动词。

items.example: It names the merging or the firming.
items.exampleCN: 它指合并或变牢这件事。

items.example: It is the same prefix in another shape.
items.exampleCN: 这是同一前缀的另一种写法。

items.example: It marks the finished state of a merged body.
items.exampleCN: 它标记合并完成后的状态。

items.example: It names the party that carries out a merger.
items.exampleCN: 它指实施合并的一方。

items.example: The finance sense needs this object to appear.
items.exampleCN: 金融义需要这类宾语才能成立。

definition_zh: 污染；玷污；使（样品、食品、环境）混入有害物
definition_en: to introduce a harmful or unwanted substance into something that was clean or pure
core_image: 一滴墨落进清水，整缸水从中心向外染成灰色
scene: 工厂把清洗溶剂的废水直接排进河里，下游的取水口被迫关闭。Waste solvent from the factory contaminated the river downstream.
sceneCN: 这里指有害物质进入水体使其不再洁净（第 1 个义项：把有害物排入水体、土壤或空气）；句意：工厂排出的废溶剂污染了下游的河水。

pos.zh: 污染；弄脏；使混入杂质；玷污

senses.title: To pollute water, soil or air
senses.definition: to put a harmful substance into the environment so that it is no longer safe
senses.definitionCN: 把有害物质排入环境，使其不再安全
senses.example: Waste solvent from the factory contaminated the river downstream.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂排出的废溶剂污染了下游的河水。
senses.why: The verb names the entry of foreign matter into something clean, and the environment is its largest stage.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词指异物进入原本洁净之物，环境是它最大的舞台。

senses.title: To infect food or a surface
senses.definition: to bring bacteria, viruses or other pathogens into food, water or a contact surface
senses.definitionCN: 把细菌、病毒或其他病原带入食物、饮水或接触表面
senses.example: Unwashed hands contaminated the sandwiches on the counter.
senses.exampleCN: 没洗的手污染了柜台上的三明治。
senses.why: Once the intruder is a living organism, contamination becomes infection, and the same verb covers it.
senses.whyCN: 一旦入侵者是活的生物体，污染就变成传染，同一个动词仍然管用。

senses.title: To spoil a scientific sample
senses.definition: to mix an unwanted substance into a sample so that a measurement no longer reflects the original
senses.definitionCN: 把不需要的物质混入样品，使测量结果不再反映原状
senses.example: A dirty pipette contaminated the blood sample.
senses.exampleCN: 一支不干净的吸管污染了血液样本。
senses.why: Laboratory work lives on purity, so the smallest intruder ruins the sample and the verb is used constantly.
senses.whyCN: 实验室工作依赖纯净，最小的入侵物就能毁掉样品，因此这个动词被频繁使用。

senses.title: To corrupt a language or culture
senses.definition: to mix foreign or inferior elements into a language, tradition or style until its character changes
senses.definitionCN: 把外来或低劣成分混入语言、传统或风格，使其性质改变
senses.example: Purists complained that slang contaminated the written language.
senses.exampleCN: 纯粹主义者抱怨俚语污染了书面语言。
senses.why: A language is imagined as a clear liquid, and borrowed elements as the drop of ink that darkens it.
senses.whyCN: 语言被想象成一缸清水，借入的成分则是把它染深的那滴墨。

senses.title: To pollute a dataset
senses.definition: to insert wrong, duplicated or irrelevant records into a dataset so that its results cannot be trusted
senses.definitionCN: 把错误、重复或无关的记录放进数据集，使结果不可信赖
senses.example: A faulty sensor contaminated the climate records for two years.
senses.exampleCN: 一个故障传感器污染了整整两年的气候记录。
senses.why: Data is treated like a sample: one bad entry spreads through every calculation made from it.
senses.whyCN: 数据被当作样品：一条坏记录会扩散到由它得出的每一次计算。

senses.title: To make something radioactive
senses.definition: to introduce radioactive material into an object, a place or a body
senses.definitionCN: 把放射性物质带入某件物体、某个场所或某个身体
senses.example: The accident contaminated the groundwater around the plant.
senses.exampleCN: 事故使电厂周围的地下水带上了放射性。
senses.why: Radiation is invisible and travels, so it became the most feared form of contamination.
senses.whyCN: 辐射看不见又会传播，因此成了最令人恐惧的污染形式。

senses.title: To taint a mind or morals
senses.definition: to fill a person or a group with ideas considered corrupting
senses.definitionCN: 用被认为败坏的观念充满某个人或某个群体
senses.example: The pamphlet warned that foreign films contaminated the young.
senses.exampleCN: 这本小册子警告说外国电影败坏了年轻人。
senses.why: The old religious sense of moral stain survived inside the modern word for physical pollution.
senses.whyCN: 古老的宗教性「道德污损」含义，保存在现代这个表示物质污染的词语里。

senses.title: To compromise a scene or evidence
senses.titleCN: 破坏现场或证据的纯净
senses.definition: to disturb a place or a piece of evidence so that traces are lost or no longer reliable
senses.definitionCN: 搅动现场或证据，使痕迹丢失或不再可靠
senses.example: Officers who walk through the room may contaminate the crime scene.
senses.exampleCN: 走进房间的警员可能破坏犯罪现场。
senses.why: Evidence must stay as it was found, so any added trace is contamination in the legal sense.
senses.whyCN: 证据必须保持发现时的样子，因此任何新增痕迹在法律意义上都是污染。

intro.en: Contaminate comes from a Latin verb of defilement built on a noun for the stain left by contact. The link to the Latin verb for touching is widely accepted, but the exact formation of the noun is still debated, so the deeper source is marked as unsettled.
intro.cn: 本词出自一个表示玷污的拉丁动词，其基础名词指接触留下的污损。它与拉丁语中表示触碰的动词有关，这一点被广泛接受，但那个名词的具体构成仍有争议，因此更早的来源标注为未有定论。

items.en: Tangere meant to touch, and the same root stands behind English words for contact and for contagion.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为触碰，英语中表示接触与传染的词都出自同一词根。

items.en: Contamen named the defilement that contact leaves behind; its own formation and variant spellings are still discussed.
items.cn: 这个拉丁名词指接触留下的污损；它自身的构成与拼写变体至今仍有讨论。

items.en: The verb meant to defile or to make unclean, and early writers used it for religious and legal pollution.
items.cn: 这个动词意为玷污或使不洁，早期作者用它指宗教与法律意义上的污损。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the sixteenth century, when the first sense was moral and religious rather than chemical.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个动词，当时最初的义项是道德与宗教性的，而不是化学性的。

items.en: Hygiene, chemistry and microbiology later moved the word to physical pollution of water, food and samples.
items.cn: 卫生学、化学与微生物学后来把这个词转向水、食品与样品的物质污染。

items.en: Source uncertain: the derivation of the noun for contact-stain from the verb for touching is the usual account, not a settled fact, so no single ancestral form is claimed.
items.cn: 来源不确定：把表示接触污损的名词追溯到表示触碰的动词，只是通行的解释，并非定论，因此不主张单一祖形。

note.en: The first group shares the contact root or looks close to it; the second group names ways of making something impure. Contaminate is about mixing in foreign matter, while distort is about twisting a shape or a story, and the two are not interchangeable.
note.cn: 第一组共享接触词根或字形相近；第二组是使某物不纯的各种方式。本词指混入异物，扭曲类词则指扭歪形状或歪曲叙述，两者不能互换。

entries.definition: The state or the act of being made impure.
entries.definitionCN: 被弄得不纯的状态或动作。

entries.definition: The intruding substance itself, not the act.
entries.definitionCN: 指入侵的物质本身，而不是动作。

entries.definition: Touching or communication; it keeps the literal sense of the root.
entries.definitionCN: 接触或联系；保留了词根的字面义。

entries.definition: The spread of disease by contact; it names transmission, not impurity.
entries.definitionCN: 疾病经接触传播；指传播，而非不纯。

entries.definition: To make the environment dirty, usually on a large scale; it is the public word for the same act.
entries.definitionCN: 使环境变脏，通常指大规模；是同一动作的公共说法。

entries.definition: To bring a pathogen into a body; it requires a living host.
entries.definitionCN: 把病原带入身体；需要有活的宿主。

entries.definition: To spoil something with a small amount of something bad, often figuratively.
entries.definitionCN: 用少量坏东西败坏某物，常用于比喻。

entries.definition: To put a toxic substance into something that will be eaten or drunk.
entries.definitionCN: 把有毒物质放进将被吃喝的东西。

entries.definition: To add an inferior substance to a product, usually for profit.
entries.definitionCN: 为获利在产品中掺入劣质成分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the contact root, the real family and the laboratory phrases that show where the word lives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用接触词根、真实同族词，以及能显示使用场合的实验室搭配。

normal.en: The root means to touch, and the noun inside the verb means the stain that touching leaves.
normal.cn: 词根意为触碰，动词内部的名词指触碰留下的污损。

normal.en: The family runs contamination, contaminant, contaminated and decontaminate.
normal.cn: 同族词有表示污染的名词、污染物、受污染的与去除污染。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: contaminate water, contaminate a sample, contaminated food.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：污染水源、使样品受污染、受污染的食品。

normal.en: The laboratory is its home: one dirty pipette ruins a whole sample.
normal.cn: 实验室是它的主场：一支脏吸管毁掉整个样品。

normal.en: The opposite is built with a removal prefix: to decontaminate is to take the intrusion out.
normal.cn: 反义靠一个表示去除的前缀构成：去污就是把入侵物清走。

abstract.en: Picture one drop of ink falling into a glass of clear water.
abstract.cn: 想象一滴墨落进一杯清水。

abstract.en: Picture a footprint appearing on a page that was supposed to stay blank.
abstract.cn: 想象一页本该空白的纸上多出一个脚印。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour that enters a quiet town and colours every conversation.
abstract.cn: 想象一则传言进入平静的小镇，把每场谈话都染上颜色。

examples.en: Heavy metals contaminated the soil near the old factory.
examples.cn: 重金属污染了老厂附近的土壤。

examples.en: One careless handler can contaminate a whole batch of food.
examples.cn: 一个粗心的操作者就能污染整批食品。

examples.en: The virus contaminated the cell culture within days.
examples.cn: 病毒在几天之内就污染了这批细胞培养物。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肯」加「摊」加「米内特」——脏东西摊进米里，整袋都不干净：污染

root: 拉丁语「触碰」词根衍生出表示接触污损的名词，再加动词词尾构成「玷污、使不洁」；名词的具体构成仍有争议，故更早来源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a harmful outsider enters something clean, whether river, food, sample, language, dataset, body, mind or evidence.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一个动作：有害的外来者进入原本洁净之物，可以是河流、食品、样品、语言、数据集、身体、心灵或证据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop of ink entering clear water and darkening the whole glass from the centre outward.
core.cn: 核心意象：一滴墨落进清水，整缸水从中心向外染成灰色。

branches.en: THE ENVIRONMENT: water, soil and air, including the invisible spread of radiation.
branches.cn: 环境：水、土壤与空气，也包括辐射那种看不见的扩散。

branches.en: THE BODY AND THE SCENE: pathogens in food, and a crime scene no longer clean.
branches.cn: 身体与现场：食品中的病原，以及不再洁净的犯罪现场。

branches.en: THE RECORD: a spoiled sample and a polluted dataset, where one intruder ruins every reading.
branches.cn: 记录：被毁的样品与被污染的数据集，一个入侵者毁掉所有读数。

branches.en: THE CULTURE: a language or tradition mixed with foreign elements until its character changes.
branches.cn: 文化：语言或传统混入外来成分，直到性质改变。

branches.en: THE MIND: morals imagined as a clear surface that can be stained.
branches.cn: 心灵：道德被想象成一块可以被染污的洁净表面。

intro.en: Contaminate is a Latin verb of touching and defilement; its family divides into the substance that intrudes and the act of removing it.
intro.cn: 本词是一个表示触碰与玷污的拉丁动词；其词族分为入侵的物质与去除污染的动作两支。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb for touching and the noun for contact-stain are the two pieces behind the English word; the noun ending is Latin as well.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示触碰的动词与表示接触污损的名词，是英语词背后的两个构件；名词词尾同样来自拉丁语。

items.example: It marks the meeting of two substances.
items.exampleCN: 它标记两种物质的相遇。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of contact.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供接触的观念。

items.example: The noun turns contact into a stain.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词把接触变成污损。

items.example: The verb is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: It gives the Latin stem an English verb shape.
items.exampleCN: 它给拉丁词干披上英语动词外形。

items.example: It builds the name of the process.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示过程的名称。

items.meaning: the thing or person that does
items.example: It builds the name of the intruding substance.
items.exampleCN: 它构成入侵物质的名称。

items.example: It builds the verb for taking the intrusion out.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示清除入侵物的动词。

items.example: It marks the state of an object already made impure.
items.exampleCN: 它标记已被弄脏的对象状态。

definition_zh: 沉思；仔细考虑；打算；凝视
definition_en: to hold a subject in the mind for a long time, or to consider a possible action
core_image: 一个人站在划定的观象圈里，久久仰头看天，圈外的一切都被暂时隔开
scene: 棋手盯着棋盘，久久不动，把后面几步都在心里走了一遍。The old player contemplated his next three moves in silence.
sceneCN: 这里指长时间凝神思考、在心里反复推演（第 1 个义项：对某事长久而专注地思考）；句意：这位老棋手静静地沉思接下来三步棋。

senses.title: To think deeply about something
senses.titleCN: 对某事长久而专注地思考
senses.definition: to keep a subject in the mind over a stretch of time, turning it over from several sides
senses.definitionCN: 在一段时间内把某个主题留在心里，从多个方面反复打量
senses.example: The old player contemplated his next three moves in silence.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老棋手静静地沉思接下来三步棋。
senses.why: The Latin verb began as attentive watching inside a marked space, and watching turned inward becomes thinking.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词最初指在划定的空间里凝神观看，观看转向内心就成了思考。

senses.title: To consider doing something
senses.definition: to have a possible action in view, usually without having decided yet
senses.definitionCN: 把某个可能的行动放在眼前，通常尚未决定
senses.example: She is contemplating a move to another city.
senses.exampleCN: 她正在考虑搬到另一座城市。
senses.why: Once an action is held before the mind long enough to be weighed, the verb means to be thinking of doing it.
senses.whyCN: 一个行动在心头放得够久、被反复权衡，这个动词就表示打算去做。

senses.title: To gaze at something attentively
senses.definition: to look at something for a long time with full attention
senses.definitionCN: 长时间全神贯注地看某物
senses.example: He contemplated the painting without speaking for several minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 他盯着那幅画看了好几分钟，一句话也没说。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply long looking; thought is described as a kind of inner gaze.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项就是长久地看；思考被描述为一种内在的注视。

senses.title: To meditate on a sacred subject
senses.definition: in religious practice, to rest the mind on a holy truth or mystery
senses.definitionCN: 在宗教实践中，让心停留在神圣的真理或奥秘上
senses.example: The monks contemplate the mystery in silence each morning.
senses.exampleCN: 修士们每天清晨在静默中默观这一奥秘。
senses.why: Christian writers took the old verb of watching and made it the name of prayerful attention.
senses.whyCN: 基督教作者接过这个古老的观看动词，把它变成祈祷式专注之名。

senses.title: To live the contemplative life
senses.definition: to devote oneself to reflection rather than to action, as a way of life
senses.definitionCN: 把自身献给反思而非行动，作为一种生活方式
senses.example: Some traditions value the person who contemplates over the person who acts.
senses.exampleCN: 有些传统更看重沉思的人，而不是行动的人。
senses.why: When contemplation becomes a habit and a calling, the verb names a whole form of life.
senses.whyCN: 当沉思成为一种习惯与召唤，这个动词就指一整套生活方式。

senses.title: To weigh a choice before deciding
senses.definition: to compare the costs and benefits of an option before acting
senses.definitionCN: 在行动之前比较某个选项的代价与好处
senses.example: The board contemplated the merger for six months.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会对这桩合并权衡了半年。
senses.why: A choice held up and turned over in the mind is the practical form of long thought.
senses.whyCN: 把选择举起来在心里反复翻转，就是长久思考的实际形态。

senses.title: To envisage consequences
senses.definition: to think through what will follow from an action or a change
senses.definitionCN: 推想某个行动或变化会带来什么
senses.example: Before signing, he contemplated the effect on his family.
senses.exampleCN: 签字之前，他设想了这件事对家庭的影响。
senses.why: The verb looks forward as well as inward, since consequences are also something one can hold before the mind.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词既向内也向前，因为后果同样可以被摆在心头。

senses.title: Of a plan that allows for something
senses.titleCN: 方案预设、容许某种情况
senses.definition: of a plan or a rule, to have a case in view and to allow for it
senses.definitionCN: 指计划或规则已经把某种情况看在眼里并予以容许
senses.example: The agreement does not contemplate any further payment.
senses.exampleCN: 这份协议并未预设还要再付任何款项。
senses.why: Official and legal usage treats the plan itself as the one doing the thinking, which is the word's coldest extension.
senses.whyCN: 官方与法律用法把计划本身当作思考者，这是这个词最冷的一层延伸。

intro.en: Contemplate goes back to a Latin verb for watching attentively inside a space marked out for observation. The religious sense came first in English, and the everyday sense of considering an action followed.
intro.cn: 本词可追溯到拉丁语中表示在划定为观察用的空间内凝神观看的动词。英语中先出现宗教义，随后才有考虑某个行动的日常义。

items.en: Templum named a space marked out for observation and for taking auspices, and only later a temple.
items.cn: 这个拉丁名词指划出来供观察与占卜的空间，后来才指神庙。

items.en: The prefix com- meant together and marked a gathering of attention into one place.
items.cn: 前缀表示一起，标记注意力向一处集中。

items.en: The verb meant to observe within such a space, and so to give a thing one's full attention.
items.cn: 这个动词指在这样的空间里观察，因此指对某物投以全部注意力。

items.en: Christian writers used it for the prayerful attention that rests on a sacred truth.
items.cn: 基督教作者用它指停留在神圣真理上的祈祷式专注。

items.en: English borrowed it through French in the fourteenth century, first in religious prose.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪经法语借入，最早见于宗教文本。

items.en: The earlier origin of the Latin noun for the marked space is not settled, and this note concerns only that deeper layer, not the clear Latin-to-French-to-English chain.
items.cn: 拉丁语中那个表示划定空间的名词，其更早来源未有定论；这里只说明更早的一层，不涉及清楚的拉丁语经法语到英语的传递链。

note.en: The first group shares the marked-space root or its English descendants; the second group names neighbouring kinds of thinking and looking.
note.cn: 第一组共享划定空间的词根或其英语后裔；第二组是相邻的思考与观看类型。

entries.definition: The state or practice of long, quiet thought.
entries.definitionCN: 长久静思的状态或实践。

entries.definition: Given to reflection; it describes a person or a life.
entries.definitionCN: 耽于反思的；描述人或生活方式。

entries.definition: A building for worship, from the same word for a marked-out space.
entries.definitionCN: 供礼拜的建筑，出自同一个表示划定空间的名词。

entries.definition: A pattern to copy, which came through the idea of a marked or fitted piece.
entries.definitionCN: 供复制的样板，其来源经过「划好或配好的构件」这一层。

entries.definition: To weigh a question heavily; it stresses the weighing rather than the long looking.
entries.definitionCN: 反复掂量一个问题；强调权衡，而非长久观看。

entries.definition: To focus the mind, often on a spiritual subject; it is the technical word for the religious sense.
entries.definitionCN: 使心专注，常指神圣主题；是宗教义的技术说法。

entries.definition: To think in a loose, dreamy way; it lacks the deliberate attention of this word.
entries.definitionCN: 松散而梦幻地想；缺少本词那种有意的专注。

entries.definition: To take something into account before deciding; it is the plain word for sense two.
entries.definitionCN: 决定前把某事纳入考量；是第二个义项的平实说法。

entries.definition: To look long and steadily; it names the looking without the thinking.
entries.definitionCN: 长久而稳定地看；只说看，不带思考。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the marked-space root, the real family and the phrases of plans, religion and decision.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用划定空间的词根、真实同族词，以及计划、宗教与决策中的固定搭配。

normal.en: The root names a space marked out for watching, so the verb means attention held in one place.
normal.cn: 词根指为观看而划出的空间，因此动词指把注意力收在一处。

normal.en: The family runs contemplation, contemplative, contemplator and contemplatively.
normal.cn: 同族词有沉思、沉思的、沉思者与沉思地。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: contemplate a change, contemplate the future, contemplate doing something.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：考虑改变、思量未来、考虑做某事。

normal.en: The religious sense is the older English one, and the plain sense of considering an action came later.
normal.cn: 宗教义是较早的英语用法，平实的考虑行动之义较晚出现。

normal.en: Official usage says a plan contemplates a case, which is the coldest but very common extension.
normal.cn: 官方用法说某方案预设某种情况，这是最冷门却极常见的延伸。

abstract.en: Picture a circle drawn on the floor, and everything outside it going quiet.
abstract.cn: 想象地上画了一个圈，圈外的一切都安静下来。

abstract.en: Picture a coin held up and turned over many times before it is spent.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币被举起、翻转许多次，才决定花掉。

abstract.en: Picture a still pool that keeps a single image for hours.
abstract.cn: 想象一池静水，把同一个倒影留住好几个小时。

examples.en: She contemplated the offer for a week before answering.
examples.cn: 她考虑了一周才回复那个提议。

examples.en: He sat by the river and contemplated the water.
examples.cn: 他坐在河边，凝视着水面。

examples.en: The rules do not contemplate part-time workers.
examples.cn: 这些规则并未预设兼职员工的情况。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肯」加「坦普」——在划好的空地里久久看天，心里反复想：沉思、考虑

root: 拉丁语「划定供观察的空间」一词加「一起」前缀，构成「在划定处凝神观看」，再经法语进入英语；先有宗教义，后扩展为考虑与打算。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from long attentive watching to deep thought, then to considering an action, weighing a choice, foreseeing results, and finally to a plan that allows for a case.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从长久的凝神观看，走向深度思考，再到考虑某个行动、权衡选择、预想后果，最后是方案预设某种情况。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person standing inside a circle marked on the ground, looking at the sky for a long time while everything outside the circle goes quiet.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在地上划出的圆圈里，久久仰头看天，圈外的一切都安静下来。

branches.en: THE GAZE AND THE THOUGHT: long looking without, and the same attention turned inward.
branches.cn: 观看与思考：向外的长久注视，以及转向内心的同一种专注。

branches.en: THE DECISION: an action held in view, and a choice weighed before it is made.
branches.cn: 抉择：把某个行动放在眼前，以及在做出之前的权衡。

branches.en: THE RELIGIOUS AND THE PHILOSOPHICAL: prayerful attention, and a whole life given to reflection.
branches.cn: 宗教与哲思：祈祷式的专注，以及献给反思的整个人生。

branches.en: THE FORESIGHT: consequences held before the mind before one acts.
branches.cn: 预见：行动之前把后果摆在心头。

branches.en: THE DOCUMENT: a plan or rule that has a case in view and allows for it.
branches.cn: 文件：把某种情况看在眼里并予以容许的计划或规则。

intro.en: Contemplate is a Latin verb of attentive watching, built from a prefix and a noun for a marked-out space; English added its endings and later widened the meaning.
intro.cn: 本词是一个表示凝神观看的拉丁动词，由前缀与表示划定空间的名词构成；英语加上词尾，后来又扩大了含义。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies both the marked-space noun and the verb of watching; French supplies the form English borrowed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语同时提供表示划定空间的名词与表示观看的动词，法语提供英语借入的形式。

items.example: It gathers attention into one place.
items.exampleCN: 它把注意力收拢到一处。

items.meaning: a space marked out for observation
items.example: The noun supplies the setting of the gaze.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供注视的场所。

items.example: The verb is the direct ancestor of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是英语词的直接祖形。

items.example: The noun names the state the verb produces.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指动词造成的状态。

items.example: It gives the Latin stem an English verb shape.
items.exampleCN: 它给拉丁词干披上英语动词外形。

items.example: It builds the English name for the practice.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示这种实践的英语名词。

items.example: It builds the adjective for a reflective person or life.
items.exampleCN: 它构成描述爱反思的人或生活的形容词。

items.example: It builds the rare name for the person who contemplates.
items.exampleCN: 它构成罕见的、指沉思者的名词。

items.example: It turns the adjective into an adverb of manner.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成方式副词。

latinEntries.meaning: a space marked out for observation; a temple
latinEntries.meaningCN: 划出来供观察的空间；神庙

definition_zh: 汇聚；集中；（线条、光线）会聚；趋于一致
definition_en: to move toward one point or to become more alike over time
core_image: 几条从不同方向伸来的路，在一个山口前越走越窄，最后并成一条
scene: 集会开始前，人们从四面八方的街道向广场靠拢，路口越来越挤。Crowds converge on the square from every side street.
sceneCN: 这里指人群从不同方向向同一地点集中（第 2 个义项：人群或队伍从各处向一处聚集）；句意：人群从每条侧街向广场汇集。

senses.title: Of lines, roads or rivers meeting
senses.definition: of lines, routes or watercourses, to come together at a single point
senses.definitionCN: 指线条、路线或河道在同一处会合
senses.example: The two roads converge at the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 两条路在桥边交会。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to bend toward one place, and the plainest picture is two straight lines leaning in.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为朝一处弯拢，最朴素的画面就是两条直线向内倾斜。

senses.title: Of crowds gathering from different directions
senses.definition: of people or groups, to move from different directions toward one place
senses.definitionCN: 指人群或队伍从不同方向朝同一地点移动
senses.example: Crowds converge on the square from every side street.
senses.exampleCN: 人群从每条侧街向广场汇集。
senses.why: People walking in from many routes repeat the geometry of meeting lines, so the verb transfers to them.
senses.whyCN: 人从多条路线走进来，重复的正是线条会合的几何，因此这个词转用于人群。

senses.title: Of ideas or policies becoming similar
senses.definition: of ideas, styles or policies, to become more alike as differences narrow
senses.definitionCN: 指观念、风格或政策之间的差异缩小，变得更为相似
senses.example: The two parties' proposals have converged over the past year.
senses.exampleCN: 两党的提案在过去一年里趋于一致。
senses.why: Two positions that were far apart move toward each other, exactly as two lines do.
senses.whyCN: 原本相距很远的两方立场彼此靠近，正如两条线的靠拢。

senses.title: Of a sequence approaching a limit
senses.definition: in mathematics, of a series or process, to approach a fixed value as it continues
senses.definitionCN: 在数学中，指数列或过程继续下去时趋近一个固定值
senses.example: The series converges to a finite sum.
senses.exampleCN: 这个级数收敛到一个有限和。
senses.why: The mathematical sense takes the picture literally: values move closer and closer to one point.
senses.whyCN: 数学义把画面照字面使用：数值一次比一次更靠近同一点。

senses.title: Of species evolving similar traits
senses.definition: in biology, of separate lineages, to evolve similar forms in response to similar conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在生物学中，指不同谱系因相似环境而演化出相似形态
senses.example: Wings in bats and birds are a case where unrelated animals converge.
senses.exampleCN: 蝙蝠与鸟的翅膀就是不同动物趋同的一例。
senses.why: Separate lines of descent bend toward the same solution, which is the biological meaning of the word.
senses.whyCN: 不同的血统弯向同一个解决办法，这就是这个词在生物学上的含义。

senses.title: Of light rays meeting through a lens
senses.definition: of light or other rays, to be brought together at a focus
senses.definitionCN: 指光线或其他射线被带到同一个焦点
senses.example: A convex lens converges the rays onto one point.
senses.exampleCN: 凸透镜把光线会聚到一点。
senses.why: Optics made the verb technical: rays that were parallel are bent until they meet.
senses.whyCN: 光学把这个动词技术化：原本平行的射线被弯到相交。

senses.title: Of efforts settling on one conclusion
senses.titleCN: 各方努力归结到同一结论
senses.definition: of separate efforts or opinions, to arrive at the same finding or decision
senses.definitionCN: 指各自的努力或意见最终得出相同结论或决定
senses.example: Independent studies converged on the same estimate.
senses.exampleCN: 几项独立研究得出了相同的估计。
senses.why: When many lines of work end at one result, the word describes agreement as a meeting point.
senses.whyCN: 当多条工作线索终结于同一结果，这个词就把共识描述成一个会合点。

senses.title: Of forces closing in on a target
senses.definition: of military or police units, to move inward from several sides toward one objective
senses.definitionCN: 指军事或警察单位从几面同时向同一目标推进
senses.example: The units converged on the bridge from three directions.
senses.exampleCN: 各部队从三个方向向大桥合围。
senses.why: Planned movement toward one objective is the most deliberate version of lines meeting.
senses.whyCN: 有组织地朝同一目标推进，是线条会合中最具意图的一种。

intro.en: Converge comes from a Latin verb meaning to bend or turn toward, made with a prefix meaning together. English took it in the eighteenth century for geometry and optics, then widened it to people and ideas.
intro.cn: 本词出自一个表示朝某处弯转的拉丁动词，前面加了表示一起的前缀。英语在十八世纪把它用于几何与光学，后来扩展到人与观念。

items.en: Vergere meant to bend or to turn, and it also lies behind words for bending aside or turning away.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为弯、转向，英语中表示偏向或转开的词也源于它。

items.en: The prefix com- meant together, and before this verb it marked movement toward one shared place.
items.cn: 前缀表示一起，加在这个动词前，标记朝同一个共享之处移动。

items.en: The Latin verb meant to bend toward one point, and it described both paths and forces.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为朝一点弯拢，既描述路径，也描述力量。

items.en: Eighteenth-century English used it for lines meeting and for rays brought to a focus.
items.cn: 十八世纪的英语用它指线条相交，也指射线被聚到焦点。

items.en: Politics, economics and biology later borrowed the image for positions that grow alike.
items.cn: 政治、经济与生物学后来借这个意象指逐渐变得相似的立场。

note.en: The first group shares the bending root or looks close to it; the second group names neighbouring ways of meeting. Converge has the parts travelling toward each other, while confront has them already face to face in hostility.
note.cn: 第一组共享弯转词根或字形相近；第二组是相邻的会合方式。本词强调各方彼此靠近，相对类词则强调双方已经正面相对、带有敌意。

entries.definition: The coming together of lines, ideas or forces.
entries.definitionCN: 线条、观念或力量的会合。

entries.definition: Tending to meet at a point or to become alike.
entries.definitionCN: 倾向于会于一点或趋于相似的。

entries.definition: The movement apart, built on the same root with a prefix of separation.
entries.definitionCN: 分开移动，由同一词根加表示分离的前缀构成。

entries.definition: An edge or a border; its older source is a word for a rod, not for bending.
entries.definitionCN: 边缘或边界；其较早来源是表示枝条的词，与弯转无关。

entries.definition: To come into the same place; it says nothing about direction or gradual approach.
entries.definitionCN: 来到同一处；不说明方向，也不说明逐渐靠近。

entries.definition: To bring or come together; people may gather without any common point.
entries.definitionCN: 把……聚到一起；人们可以聚拢而不指向某一点。

entries.definition: To become one body; it marks the result, while this word marks the approach.
entries.definitionCN: 成为一个主体；标记结果，而本词标记靠拢过程。

entries.definition: To fall on the same point, time or opinion; it is about being identical, not moving together.
entries.definitionCN: 落在同一点、同一时刻或同一意见上；强调相同，而非一同移动。

entries.definition: To bring rays or attention to one point; it names the sharp meeting place, not the travel toward it.
entries.definitionCN: 把光线或注意力聚到一点；指会聚之处，不指靠拢过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the bending root, the real family and the fixed prepositions that show direction.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用弯转词根、真实同族词，以及能显示方向的固定介词。

normal.en: The root means to bend, so the verb pictures lines bending toward one point.
normal.cn: 词根意为弯，动词就是把线弯向一点的画面。

normal.en: The family runs convergence, convergent, converging and the opposite divergence.
normal.cn: 同族词有汇聚、汇聚的、正在汇合，以及反义的离散。

normal.en: The prepositions are on, at, toward and into, each marking a different kind of meeting.
normal.cn: 介词分别用向、在、朝与汇成，各自标记不同的会合方式。

normal.en: The optical sense is literal: a lens bends rays until they meet.
normal.cn: 光学义最字面：透镜把光线弯到相交。

normal.en: The political sense is figurative: positions that were far apart become alike.
normal.cn: 政治义是比喻：原本相距很远的立场变得相似。

abstract.en: Picture many rivers finding one sea without planning to.
abstract.cn: 想象许多河流没有约定就找到了同一片海。

abstract.en: Picture two people walking toward each other from opposite ends of a bridge.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人从桥的两端朝彼此走来。

abstract.en: Picture a dozen hands reaching for the same single switch in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗中十几只手伸向同一个开关。

examples.en: Three highways converge just north of the city.
examples.cn: 三条公路在城市北面不远处交会。

examples.en: Their views gradually converged during the talks.
examples.cn: 在会谈期间，他们的看法逐渐趋于一致。

examples.en: The two species converged in body shape without being close relatives.
examples.cn: 这两个物种并非近亲，体型却趋同了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肯」加「涡奇」——几条路拐着弯挤到同一个山口：汇聚、趋同

root: 拉丁语「弯、转向」动词加「一起」前缀，构成「朝一点弯拢」，十八世纪进入英语的几何与光学，后扩展到人群、观念与物种。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from lines meeting through crowds and ideas to limits, species, light, shared conclusions and closing forces.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从线条交会开始，经人群与观念，走到极限、物种、光线、共同结论与合围的部队。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several roads coming from different directions, narrowing as they near one mountain pass and finally joining into one.
core.cn: 核心意象：几条从不同方向伸来的路，在一个山口前越走越窄，最后并成一条。

branches.en: THE GEOMETRY: roads, rivers and drawn lines arriving at one point.
branches.cn: 几何：道路、河流与画出的线条抵达同一点。

branches.en: THE CROWD: people moving in from many directions toward one place.
branches.cn: 人群：人从许多方向朝同一地点移动。

branches.en: THE SHARED POSITION: ideas growing alike, and separate efforts reaching one conclusion.
branches.cn: 共同立场：观念变得相似，各项努力得出同一结论。

branches.en: THE TECHNICAL FOCUS: a series approaching a limit, and rays brought to a focus.
branches.cn: 技术性会聚：数列趋近极限，射线被聚到焦点。

branches.en: THE NATURAL AND THE PLANNED: evolution producing similar forms, and units closing in on a target.
branches.cn: 自然与筹划：演化产出相似形态，部队向目标合围。

intro.en: Converge is a Latin verb of bending toward, and its English family supplies the noun, the adjective and the opposite formed with a prefix of separation.
intro.cn: 本词是一个表示朝某处弯转的拉丁动词，其英语词族提供名词、形容词，以及由表示分离的前缀构成的反义词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vergere and the prefix com- form the whole verb; English added only endings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示弯转的动词与表示一起的前缀构成整个动词，英语只加了词尾。

items.example: It turns bending into bending together.
items.exampleCN: 它把弯转变成一起弯拢。

items.example: The root supplies the direction of movement.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供运动的方向。

items.example: The verb is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: English shortened the Latin verb to its modern shape.
items.exampleCN: 英语把拉丁动词缩短成现代形式。

items.example: It builds the noun for the meeting of lines.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示线条会合的名词。

items.example: It builds the adjective for things that come together.
items.exampleCN: 它构成描述趋向会合之物的形容词。

items.example: It builds the opposite verb for moving apart.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示分开移动的反义动词。

items.example: It marks movement that is still under way.
items.exampleCN: 它标记仍在进行中的移动。

items.example: It marks lines that have already met.
items.exampleCN: 它标记已经会合的线条。

latinEntries.meaning: to bend together toward a point

definition_zh: （使）相关；使相互关联；对应；并置比对
definition_en: to have a mutual relation, or to place two sets of things so that they match
core_image: 两条曲线画在同一张方格纸上，一条升高时另一条也跟着升高，起落彼此对齐
scene: 研究者把十年的降雨记录与河流流量并排画在同一张图上，两条线几乎同步起落。Researchers correlate rainfall records with river flow over ten years.
sceneCN: 这里指把两组记录并排摆放，使对应项彼此对齐（第 5 个义项：把两组数据或记录对齐比对）；句意：研究者把十年的降雨记录与河流流量对应起来看。

senses.title: Of two things varying together
senses.definition: of two quantities or facts, to change together in a way that can be observed
senses.definitionCN: 指两个数量或事实以可观察的方式一同变化
senses.example: Height and weight correlate across the whole population.
senses.exampleCN: 在整个人群中，身高与体重是相关的。
senses.why: The prefix means together and the root means carried back, so two things are carried back to each other.
senses.whyCN: 前缀表示一起，词根表示带回，因此两样东西彼此被带回对照。

senses.title: To show a statistical correlation
senses.definition: to establish by measurement that two variables move together more than chance would explain
senses.definitionCN: 通过测量确定两个变量的同向变化超出偶然所能解释的范围
senses.example: The survey correlates income with years of schooling.
senses.exampleCN: 这项调查把收入与受教育年限联系起来。
senses.why: Statistics turned the mutual relation into a coefficient, and the verb took on the measuring sense.
senses.whyCN: 统计学把相互关联变成一个系数，这个动词也就有了测量的含义。

senses.title: To connect things in the mind
senses.titleCN: 在心里把事物联系起来
senses.definition: to bring two ideas into a mental link so that one calls up the other
senses.definitionCN: 把两个观念在心里连起来，使一个能唤起另一个
senses.example: Children correlate the sound of the bell with the end of class.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们把铃声与下课联系起来。
senses.why: The mind carries one idea back to another, which is the same movement the Latin root names.
senses.whyCN: 心智把一个观念带回另一个，这正是那个拉丁词根所命名的动作。

senses.title: To correspond to each other
senses.definition: of two series or accounts, to match item by item so that each has a partner
senses.definitionCN: 指两个序列或两份陈述逐项吻合，各自都有对应项
senses.example: The numbered seals correlate with the entries in the catalogue.
senses.exampleCN: 带编号的印章与目录中的条目一一对应。
senses.why: The preposition with marks the second term of the pair, and the verb simply reports that the pair fits.
senses.whyCN: 介词标明这一对中的第二项，动词只报告这一对彼此吻合。

senses.title: To line up two sets of records
senses.definition: to arrange two sets of data or documents so that matching items stand side by side
senses.definitionCN: 把两组数据或文件排列好，使相配的项目彼此并排
senses.example: Researchers correlate rainfall records with river flow over ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者把十年的降雨记录与河流流量对应起来看。
senses.why: Records are correlated when one column is laid against another, which is the manual act behind the statistics.
senses.whyCN: 当一列数据对着另一列摆好，记录就被对齐了，这是统计背后的手工动作。

senses.title: To match rock layers across regions
senses.titleCN: 把不同地区的岩层对应起来
senses.definition: in geology, to identify layers in separate places as the same age or origin
senses.definitionCN: 在地质学中，判定不同地点的地层属于同一时代或同一来源
senses.example: Geologists correlate the sandstone beds on both sides of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 地质学家把河谷两侧的砂岩层对应起来。
senses.why: Strata are matched by their fossils and grain, the same lining-up act carried out on a landscape.
senses.whyCN: 地层靠化石与颗粒特征配对，就是把对齐动作放到整片地貌上。

senses.title: Of traits that vary together in species
senses.definition: in biology, of two traits or structures, to occur together across related organisms
senses.definitionCN: 在生物学中，指两种性状或结构在亲缘生物中相伴出现
senses.example: Wing length and body size correlate in these birds.
senses.exampleCN: 在这些鸟身上，翅长与体型大小是相关的。
senses.why: Living things supply paired measurements too, so the statistical sense extends to natural variation.
senses.whyCN: 生物同样提供成对的测量值，统计义便延伸到自然变异。

senses.title: To compare findings across studies
senses.titleCN: 在多项研究之间做对应比较
senses.definition: to bring results from separate studies into one comparison so that agreement or conflict shows
senses.definitionCN: 把不同研究的结果放进同一次比较，使一致或冲突之处显现
senses.example: The review correlates the findings of twelve field studies.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇综述把十二项实地研究的发现对应比较。
senses.why: Research synthesis is a large-scale version of laying two records side by side.
senses.whyCN: 研究综合就是把两份记录并排摆放这一动作的放大版。

intro.en: Correlate joins a prefix meaning together to the Latin participle of the verb for carrying back. Medieval Latin used the pair for things that answer to each other, and statistics gave the word its modern measuring sense.
intro.cn: 本词把表示一起的前缀接在拉丁语中表示带回的动词分词上。中世纪拉丁语用这一对词指彼此呼应之物，统计学又给了它现代的测量含义。

items.en: Referre meant to carry back or to bring into relation, and its participle is the second half of this word.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为带回或使发生关联，它的分词就是本词的后半截。

items.en: The prefix com- meant together, so the compound said carried back together, that is, set in a mutual relation.
items.cn: 前缀表示一起，因此复合词意为被一起带回，也就是被摆进相互关系。

items.en: Medieval Latin used the form for things that correspond, especially in grammar and theology.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语用这个形式指彼此对应之物，尤其见于语法与神学。

items.en: Nineteenth-century statistics made correlation a measured relation between two variables.
items.cn: 十九世纪的统计学把相关变成两个变量之间可测量的关系。

items.en: English took the verb in the nineteenth century, chiefly in scientific and academic writing.
items.cn: 英语在十九世纪借入这个动词，主要用于科学与学术写作。

items.en: Geology, biology and research synthesis later applied the same alignment to strata, traits and whole studies.
items.cn: 地质学、生物学与研究综合后来把同一种对齐动作用于地层、性状与整项研究。

note.en: The first group shares the carrying-back root or its family forms; the second group names nearby kinds of matching. Correlate reports that two things vary or line up together, while corroborate reports that evidence makes a claim stronger, so relation and proof must not be confused.
note.cn: 第一组共享带回词根或其词族形式；第二组是相邻的配对类型。本词说的是两件事一同变化或彼此对齐，佐证类词说的是证据把某个说法坐实，关系与证明不能混为一谈。

entries.definition: The measured relation between two things, or the act of aligning them.
entries.definitionCN: 两事物之间被测量的关系，或把它们对齐的动作。

entries.definition: Mutually related, and in grammar a paired word such as either and or.
entries.definitionCN: 相互关联的；语法上指成对出现的词。

entries.definition: Considered in relation to something else; it stops short of measuring a pair.
entries.definitionCN: 相对于某物而言的；并未达到测量一对关系的程度。

entries.definition: To connect or to tell; it is the plainer verb behind the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 连接或讲述；是名词背后更平实的动词。

entries.definition: To match or to exchange letters; matching is by form or position, not by measured variation.
entries.definitionCN: 相配或通信；匹配依据形式或位置，而非测量出的共同变化。

entries.definition: To link in thought or in company; no measurement is implied.
entries.definitionCN: 在思想上或交往中联系；不牵涉测量。

entries.definition: To join or to show a link; it is the general word for any linkage.
entries.definitionCN: 连接或显示联系；是任何联系的泛称。

entries.definition: To put two things together because they are alike; the judgement is identity, not variation.
entries.definitionCN: 因相似而把两物配在一起；判断的是相同，而非共变。

entries.definition: To fall on the same point or time; coincidence is exact, correlation is statistical.
entries.definitionCN: 落在同一点或同一时刻；重合是精确的，相关是统计的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the carrying-back root, the real family and the preposition that marks the second term.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用带回词根、真实同族词，以及标记第二项的介词。

normal.en: The root means carried back, so two things are carried back to each other for comparison.
normal.cn: 词根意为带回，两样东西被带回到彼此面前作比较。

normal.en: The family runs correlation, correlative, correlated and correlational.
normal.cn: 同族词有相关、对应的、相关的与相关性研究的。

normal.en: The preposition is with: one thing correlates with another.
normal.cn: 介词用与：一事物与另一事物相关。

normal.en: Statistics supplies the number, but the everyday sense needs no number at all.
normal.cn: 统计学提供数值，但日常义完全不需要数值。

normal.en: The geological sense is a large-scale version: whole layers matched across a valley.
normal.cn: 地质义是放大版：整层岩层跨越河谷彼此对应。

abstract.en: Picture two dancers who never touch but always turn at the same moment.
abstract.cn: 想象两名舞者从不接触，却总在同一瞬间转身。

abstract.en: Picture two clocks in different rooms that keep the same error.
abstract.cn: 想象两个房间里的两只钟犯着同样的误差。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow that lengthens exactly as the person grows.
abstract.cn: 想象影子随着人的长高而变长。

examples.en: Income does not always correlate with happiness.
examples.cn: 收入并不总与幸福感相关。

examples.en: The two lists correlate neatly once the dates are aligned.
examples.cn: 把日期对齐之后，两份清单便整齐地对应起来。

examples.en: Researchers correlate soil acidity with crop yield.
examples.cn: 研究者把土壤酸度与作物产量对应起来分析。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可」加「瑞」加「累特」——两条线一起起落，像被同一根绳拉着：相关

root: 拉丁语「带回」动词的分词加「一起」前缀，中世纪拉丁语指彼此对应之物，十九世纪经统计学获得「相关」的测量含义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one alignment: variables varying together, a measured coefficient, mental association, item-by-item matching, records laid side by side, rock layers, paired traits and pooled studies.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一种对齐：变量共同变化、测出的系数、心里的联想、逐项对应、并排的记录、岩层、成对的性状，以及汇总的研究。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two curves drawn on one sheet of graph paper, rising and falling together.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条曲线画在同一张方格纸上，一条升高时另一条也跟着升高，起落彼此对齐。

branches.en: THE MEASURED RELATION: things varying together, and the coefficient that records it.
branches.cn: 被测量的关系：事物共同变化，以及记录它的系数。

branches.en: THE MIND: one idea calling up another without any number.
branches.cn: 心智：一个观念唤起另一个，不涉及数值。

branches.en: THE ALIGNMENT: series corresponding item by item, and records laid side by side.
branches.cn: 对齐：序列逐项对应，记录并排摆放。

branches.en: THE NATURAL WORLD: rock layers matched across a valley and traits paired across a species.
branches.cn: 自然世界：跨越河谷对应的岩层，以及物种中成对的性状。

branches.en: THE LITERATURE: separate studies brought into one comparison.
branches.cn: 文献：多项研究被放进同一次比较。

intro.en: Correlate is a Latin compound of togetherness and carrying back, and its family supplies the noun, the adjective and the plainer verb of relation.
intro.cn: 本词是表示「一起」与「带回」的拉丁复合词，其词族提供名词、形容词，以及更平实的关联动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin referre and its participle relatus supply the second half; com- supplies the first.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示带回的动词及其分词提供后半截，前缀提供前半截。

items.example: It makes the carrying mutual.
items.exampleCN: 它使「带回」成为相互的。

items.example: The verb supplies the second half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供复合词的后半截。

items.example: The participle is the shape English actually took over.
items.exampleCN: 英语实际接收的是这个分词形式。

items.example: Medieval writers added the prefix to the participle.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪作者在这个分词前加了前缀。

items.example: It turns the Latin stem into the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 它把拉丁词干变成英语动词。

items.example: It builds the name of the measured relation.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示被测量关系的名词。

items.example: It builds the adjective for paired items.
items.exampleCN: 它构成描述成对项目的形容词。

items.example: It builds the adjective for studies of correlation.
items.exampleCN: 它构成描述相关性研究的形容词。

items.example: The pair needs this preposition to name its second term.
items.exampleCN: 这一对需要这个介词引出第二项。

latinEntries.meaning: to carry back, to bring into relation

definition_zh: 证实；佐证；以证据支持（说法、理论、证词）
definition_en: to strengthen a statement or a finding by adding independent evidence
core_image: 一根细木柱旁再立一根粗橡木，两根顶住同一块石板，石板便不再晃动
scene: 两名独立目击者的记录摆上桌面，关键时间点彼此吻合。Two independent records corroborate the driver's account of the accident.
sceneCN: 这里指用独立材料支持某项陈述（第 1 个义项：以独立证据证实某个说法）；句意：两份独立记录证实了司机对这起事故的陈述。

senses.title: To confirm a statement with other evidence
senses.definition: to support a person's account by producing evidence that did not come from that person
senses.definitionCN: 用并非出自陈述者之手的证据来支持其说法
senses.example: Two independent records corroborate the driver's account of the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 两份独立记录证实了司机对这起事故的陈述。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to strengthen, and a statement is strengthened when something outside it holds it up.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为使强壮，当陈述之外的东西把它撑住，它就被加强了。

senses.title: To support a theory with further evidence
senses.definition: to give a hypothesis additional support from data or experiment
senses.definitionCN: 用数据或实验为假说提供额外支持
senses.example: Later observations corroborated the model's prediction.
senses.exampleCN: 后来的观测印证了该模型的预测。
senses.why: A theory is a load-bearing claim, so evidence that holds it up is pictured as physical support.
senses.whyCN: 理论是一项承重的断言，因此支撑它的证据被想象成物理支撑。

senses.title: To strengthen physically (old sense)
senses.titleCN: 使身体或结构变强壮（古义）
senses.definition: in older usage, to make a body or a structure stronger
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中，指使身体或结构更强壮
senses.example: The old tonic was said to corroborate the constitution.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的补药据说能强健体质。
senses.why: The literal sense survives from Latin, where the root named strength itself, and medicine kept it longest.
senses.whyCN: 字面义来自拉丁语，那里的词根就指力量，医学把它保留得最久。

senses.title: To back a witness's testimony in law
senses.definition: in law, to support a witness's testimony with independent proof so that it can be relied on
senses.definitionCN: 在法律上以独立证明支持证人证词，使其可以采信
senses.example: The passport record corroborates her account of the journey.
senses.exampleCN: 护照记录印证了她对那次行程的叙述。
senses.why: Courts distrust a single voice, so a second source that supports it has a fixed name and a fixed role.
senses.whyCN: 法庭不相信孤立的一家之言，因此支持它的第二个来源有固定名称与固定作用。

senses.title: To confirm a result by replication
senses.definition: to confirm a result by obtaining it again independently
senses.definitionCN: 通过独立地再次得到同一结果来证实它
senses.example: Three laboratories corroborated the original finding.
senses.exampleCN: 三家实验室证实了最初的结果。
senses.why: Replication is the modern form of adding a second pillar under a slab.
senses.whyCN: 重复实验就是给石板再加一根支柱的现代形式。

senses.title: To back a rumour or suspicion with facts
senses.titleCN: 用事实支撑传闻或怀疑
senses.definition: to give a rumour enough factual support that it can no longer be dismissed
senses.definitionCN: 给传闻足够的真实依据，使其不再能被轻易否定
senses.example: Phone records corroborated the suspicion that had circulated for weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 通话记录支持了流传数周的怀疑。
senses.why: The verb is neutral about the claim's truth; it reports that the support is there.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词对说法是否真实保持中立，只报告支撑确实存在。

senses.title: To support someone's version of events
senses.titleCN: 支持某人对事件的叙述
senses.definition: to confirm the particular version of events that one person has given
senses.definitionCN: 确认某个人所给出的那一版事件经过
senses.example: Two neighbours corroborated his version of the night.
senses.exampleCN: 两位邻居印证了他对那一夜的叙述。
senses.why: The object is a person's version rather than a fact, which is why the verb so often takes an account as its object.
senses.whyCN: 宾语是某人的版本而不是一个事实，因此这个动词常以叙述为宾语。

senses.title: Of a detail that fits and strengthens
senses.definition: of a small detail, to fit the rest of the picture so well that it strengthens the whole
senses.definitionCN: 指某个小细节与整体情况吻合得足以加强整体
senses.example: The date on the ticket corroborates the story in one small point.
senses.exampleCN: 票上的日期在一个小点上印证了那套说法。
senses.why: A single detail can act as a second pillar if it is independent and precise.
senses.whyCN: 只要独立而精确，一个细节也能充当第二根支柱。

intro.en: Corroborate comes from a Latin verb meaning to strengthen, built on the Latin word for oak and for strength. English took it in the sixteenth century, and law and science later specialized its use.
intro.cn: 本词出自一个表示使强壮的拉丁动词，其词根指橡木，也指力量。英语在十六世纪借入，法律与科学后来把它的用法专门化。

items.en: Robur meant oak and, by extension, strength or the strongest part of anything.
items.cn: 这个拉丁名词指橡木，引申指力量，或任何事物最坚固的部分。

items.en: The prefix com- added intensity, so the compound meant to strengthen thoroughly.
items.cn: 前缀加强语气，因此复合词意为彻底使强壮。

items.en: The Latin verb meant to give strength, and it could be used of bodies, buildings and arguments alike.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为给予力量，既可用于身体与建筑，也可用于论证。

items.en: English borrowed it in the sixteenth century, when strengthening a claim with proof was already a courtroom habit.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入，当时用证据加固说法已是法庭习惯。

items.en: Testimony, then experiment, gave the word its two technical homes.
items.cn: 先是证词，后是实验，给了这个词两个技术归宿。

items.en: Replication turned the old image of a second pillar into the standard test of a finding.
items.cn: 重复实验把「第二根支柱」的古老意象变成检验研究结果的标准做法。

note.en: The first group shares the oak-and-strength root or looks close to it; the second group names nearby kinds of proof. Corroborate adds independent support, whereas correlate only reports that two things vary together, and a correlation by itself proves nothing about cause.
note.cn: 第一组共享橡木与力量的词根或字形相近；第二组是相邻的证明方式。本词指加上独立支撑，而相关类词只报告两事物共同变化，单靠相关并不能证明因果。

entries.definition: The independent support that makes a claim hold.
entries.definitionCN: 使说法立得住的独立支撑。

entries.definition: Serving as such support, as in corroborative detail.
entries.definitionCN: 起这种支撑作用的，如佐证性的细节。

entries.definition: Strong and hard to break; it describes the object, not the proof.
entries.definitionCN: 强壮而不易损坏；描述对象本身，而非证明。

entries.definition: The person or source that supplies the support.
entries.definitionCN: 提供支撑的人或来源。

entries.definition: To make a claim certain; it reports the result, while this word reports the added support.
entries.definitionCN: 使说法确定；报告结果，而本词报告外加的支撑。

entries.definition: To check that something is true; the checking is the point, not the added strength.
entries.definitionCN: 核查某事是否属实；重点在核查，而非加固。

entries.definition: To give a claim enough substance to stand; it stresses material rather than a second pillar.
entries.definitionCN: 给说法足够的实质使其站住；强调实质，而非第二根支柱。

entries.definition: To hold something up generally; it is the wider word behind the technical one.
entries.definitionCN: 一般性地撑住某物；是技术词背后更宽泛的说法。

entries.definition: To establish that something is sound or acceptable, often by a formal procedure.
entries.definitionCN: 确认某物可靠或可接受，常通过正式程序。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the oak-and-strength root, the real family and the legal phrases that fix the word's role.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用橡木与力量的词根、真实同族词，以及固定其作用的法律搭配。

normal.en: The root names oak, the hardest wood, so the verb means to give a claim the strength of oak.
normal.cn: 词根指橡木这种最硬的木材，因此动词意为给说法以橡木般的力量。

normal.en: The family runs corroboration, corroborative, corroborator and the related adjective robust.
normal.cn: 同族词有佐证、佐证性的、提供佐证者，以及同根的「强壮」形容词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: corroborate a story, corroborate testimony, corroborating evidence.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：证实说法、印证证词、佐证材料。

normal.en: The courtroom is its oldest home: a second source under a single voice.
normal.cn: 法庭是它最早的主场：给孤证再加一个来源。

normal.en: Replication is its laboratory form: the same result found again elsewhere.
normal.cn: 重复实验是它的实验室形态：别处再次得到同一结果。

abstract.en: Picture a leaning wall held up by a second beam placed beside the first.
abstract.cn: 想象一面将倒的墙，被并与第一根梁的第二根梁撑住。

abstract.en: Picture two witnesses who never met telling the same small detail.
abstract.cn: 想象两个从未见面的证人说出同一个细节。

abstract.en: Picture a bridge cable that only holds when a second cable takes the strain.
abstract.cn: 想象一根桥索只有在第二根分担拉力时才撑得住。

examples.en: The letters corroborate her account of the escape.
examples.cn: 这些信件印证了她对那次出逃的叙述。

examples.en: No independent source corroborates the claim.
examples.cn: 没有独立来源能佐证这一说法。

examples.en: Two experiments corroborated the earlier result.
examples.cn: 两项实验证实了早先的结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「可」加「若伯」——再立一根橡木柱子顶住，说法就稳了：证实、佐证

root: 拉丁语「橡木、力量」一词加加强前缀构成「使强壮」，十六世纪进入英语；先用于证词，后用于实验与证据。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all add a second support: a statement, a theory, an old body, a witness, a replicated result, a rumour, a personal version and a single detail.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在加第二重支撑：说法、理论、旧时的身体、证人、被重复的结果、传闻、个人叙述与单个细节。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a second pillar of hard oak placed beside the first under one stone slab, and the slab stops shaking.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细木柱旁再立一根粗橡木，两根顶住同一块石板，石板便不再晃动。

branches.en: THE ACCOUNT: a statement or a person's version held up from outside.
branches.cn: 叙述：一个说法或某人的版本由外部撑住。

branches.en: THE THEORY: a hypothesis supported, and a result found again elsewhere.
branches.cn: 理论：假说得到支持，结果在别处再次得到。

branches.en: THE OLD BODY: the literal sense of making a constitution stronger.
branches.cn: 旧时的身体：使体质变强的字面义。

branches.en: THE COURT: a single voice given a second independent source.
branches.cn: 法庭：孤立的一家之言得到第二个独立来源。

branches.en: THE SMALL SUPPORT: a rumour backed by facts, or one precise detail that fits.
branches.cn: 细小支撑：传闻得到事实支持，或一个精确吻合的细节。

intro.en: Corroborate is a Latin verb of strength, and its family supplies the noun of support, the adjective of supporting detail and the related adjective for sheer toughness.
intro.cn: 本词是一个表示力量的拉丁动词，其词族提供表示支撑的名词、描述佐证细节的形容词，以及描述单纯坚固的同根形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin robur and the intensive prefix are the two pieces of the verb; the English endings are added on top.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示橡木与力量的词，加上加强前缀，构成这个动词的两个构件，英语词尾再加在外面。

items.example: It makes the strengthening thorough.
items.exampleCN: 它使「加强」变得彻底。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of hardness.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供坚硬之意。

items.example: The verb is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: It gives the Latin stem an English verb shape.
items.exampleCN: 它给拉丁词干披上英语动词外形。

items.example: It builds the name of the added support.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示外加支撑的名词。

items.example: It builds the adjective for evidence that supports.
items.exampleCN: 它构成描述支持性证据的形容词。

items.example: It builds a rare adjective of the same kind.
items.exampleCN: 它构成同类的罕见形容词。

items.example: It builds the name of the supporting source.
items.exampleCN: 它构成提供支撑者的名称。

items.example: The verb almost always works on proof or on a statement.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词几乎总是作用于证明或说法。

definition_en: to act against something so that its effect is reduced or cancelled
core_image: 两股等大的力从相反方向推同一扇门，门纹丝不动
scene: 医生在开第一种药的同时加上第二种，把前者的副作用压回去。The second drug counteracts the side effects of the first.
sceneCN: 这里指用一种物质中和另一种物质的作用（第 2 个义项：用药物或化学品抵消某种效应）；句意：第二种药抵消了第一种药的副作用。

senses.title: To act against an effect
senses.definition: to act in opposition to something so that its force is weakened
senses.definitionCN: 采取相反的行动，使某种力量被削弱
senses.example: The safety valve counteracts the rise in pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 安全阀抵消了压力的上升。
senses.why: The word is built from against and act, so the picture is one action meeting another action head on.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由「相反」与「行动」构成，画面就是一个动作迎面遇上另一个动作。

senses.title: To neutralize a drug or chemical
senses.titleCN: 中和药物或化学品的作用
senses.definition: to oppose the physiological effect of a substance with another substance
senses.definitionCN: 用另一种物质对抗某种物质的生理效应
senses.example: The second drug counteracts the side effects of the first.
senses.exampleCN: 第二种药抵消了第一种药的副作用。
senses.why: Medicine applied the against-action to bodies, where one substance can cancel what another does.
senses.whyCN: 医学把这种反向作用用到身体上，一种物质能取消另一种物质造成的效果。

senses.title: To counteract inflation or a trend
senses.definition: to act against an economic movement by policy or by market response
senses.definitionCN: 用政策或市场反应对抗某种经济走势
senses.example: The central bank raised rates to counteract inflation.
senses.exampleCN: 中央银行提高利率以抑制通货膨胀。
senses.why: An economy has momentum, and policy is described as a hand pushing the other way.
senses.whyCN: 经济有惯性，政策就被描述成一只朝反方向推的手。

senses.title: To offset harmful effects by measures
senses.definition: to introduce measures that answer the bad consequences of an action
senses.definitionCN: 采取配套措施，回应某项行动带来的坏后果
senses.example: The new rules counteract the damage done by earlier cuts.
senses.exampleCN: 新规则抵消了早先削减造成的损害。
senses.why: The verb is neutral about method: any measure that pushes back counts as acting against the effect.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词对方法保持中立：任何回推的措施都算作对抗该效应。

senses.title: To counter an influence or propaganda
senses.definition: to reduce the force of an influence by offering a rival influence
senses.definitionCN: 通过提供对立的影响来削弱某种影响的力量
senses.example: The campaign tried to counteract rumours spread online.
senses.exampleCN: 这场宣传活动试图抵消网上流传的谣言。
senses.why: Influence is imagined as pressure from one side, so answering it is pressure from the other.
senses.whyCN: 影响被想象成一面来的压力，回应它就是从另一面施加压力。

senses.title: To oppose a physical force
senses.definition: to balance or cancel a force such as gravity, thrust or drag
senses.definitionCN: 平衡或取消重力、推力、阻力等力
senses.example: The thrust counteracts gravity during the hover.
senses.exampleCN: 悬停时，推力抵消了重力。
senses.why: Physics gives the clearest version: two vectors equal and opposite, and nothing moves.
senses.whyCN: 物理学给出最清楚的版本：两个大小相等方向相反的矢量，结果纹丝不动。

senses.title: To thwart someone's plans
senses.definition: to act so as to prevent another person's plan from succeeding
senses.definitionCN: 采取行动使另一个人的计划无法成功
senses.example: The rival firm counteracted the merger plan with a better offer.
senses.exampleCN: 对手公司用更优厚的报价挫败了那项合并计划。
senses.why: A plan is an action aimed at a result, so an action aimed against it is the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 计划是朝着某个结果的行动，针对它的行动自然就用同一个动词。

senses.title: To counteract corrosion or wear
senses.definition: to slow or prevent the chemical or mechanical decay of a material
senses.definitionCN: 减缓或阻止材料的化学或机械劣化
senses.example: A protective coating counteracts corrosion in the pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 保护涂层抑制了管道内的腐蚀。
senses.why: Materials science treats decay as an active process, so opposing it is a form of action.
senses.whyCN: 材料科学把劣化视为一个主动过程，因此对抗它也是一种行动。

intro.en: Counteract is an English-made compound, not a borrowed Latin verb: the prefix of opposition was joined to the verb for acting, following a Latin pattern. English had it by the fifteenth century.
intro.cn: 本词是英语自造的复合动词，而非整体借入的拉丁动词：表示相反的前缀接在表示行动的动词上，依照拉丁语的构词模式。英语在十五世纪已有此词。

items.en: Contra meant against or opposite, and it entered English as a prefix of opposition.
items.cn: 这个拉丁词意为相反、对着，进入英语后成为表示对立的前缀。

items.en: Agere meant to do or to drive, and its participle actum gave English the verb to act.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为做、推动，其分词给英语提供了「行动」这个动词。

items.en: English joined the prefix to the verb rather than borrowing a Latin compound whole; the model was Latin, the making was English.
items.cn: 英语把这个前缀接到这个动词上，而不是整体借入某个拉丁复合词；模式来自拉丁语，制造过程是英语的。

items.en: The verb appears from the fifteenth century in the sense of acting against a force or an effect.
items.cn: 这个动词自十五世纪起出现，义为对抗某种力量或效应。

items.en: Medicine, economics, propaganda and materials science each gave the old pattern a new object.
items.cn: 医学、经济学、宣传与材料科学各自给这个古老模式配上了新宾语。

note.en: The first group shares the against-prefix or the act root; the second group names nearby ways of cancelling an effect. Counteract is a verb of action against an effect, while contaminate is a verb of introducing impurity, so they belong to different fields.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示相反的前缀或行动词根；第二组是相邻的取消效应方式。本词强调以行动对抗某种效应，污染类词强调引入杂质，分属不同领域。

entries.definition: The act of pushing back against an effect.
entries.definitionCN: 对抗某种效应的动作。

entries.definition: Having the power to oppose an effect.
entries.definitionCN: 具有对抗某种效应之力的。

entries.definition: To weigh against something so that balance is restored; it stresses equilibrium, not action.
entries.definitionCN: 以对等的重量使平衡恢复；强调平衡，而非行动。

entries.definition: A prefix of opposition, and also a shop counter; only the prefix sense is shared here.
entries.definitionCN: 表示对立的前缀，也指柜台；这里只共享前缀义。
