entries.definition: To balance one effect with another; the two may cancel without direct opposition.
entries.definitionCN: 用一种效应平衡另一种效应；两者可以不直接对立而相消。

entries.definition: To make something ineffective; it stresses the result of no effect rather than the opposing act.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物失效；强调无效的结果，而非对抗动作。

entries.definition: To cancel or make null; it is often logical or total.
entries.definitionCN: 取消或使归零；常用于逻辑或彻底否定。

entries.definition: To block a plan or a person; the object is an intention, not a physical effect.
entries.definitionCN: 阻挠计划或人；宾语是意图，而非物理效应。

entries.definition: To be against something; it names the stance, not the cancelling of an effect.
entries.definitionCN: 反对某事物；指立场，而非取消效应。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real prefix, the real verb and the fixed objects that show what can be acted against.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实前缀、真实动词，以及能显示可对抗对象范围的固定搭配。

normal.en: The prefix means against, the verb means act, so the word means act against.
normal.cn: 前缀意为相反，动词意为行动，合起来就是反向行动。

normal.en: The family runs counteraction, counteractive and counteragent.
normal.cn: 同族词有抵消、起抵消作用的与对抗剂。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: counteract the effects, counteract inflation, counteract corrosion.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：抵消影响、抑制通胀、抑制腐蚀。

normal.en: The physics case is the clearest: equal and opposite forces, and nothing moves.
normal.cn: 物理情形最清楚：等大反向的力，结果不动。

normal.en: The word is English-made on a Latin pattern, which is why it looks like a prefix simply placed before a verb.
normal.cn: 这个词是英语按拉丁模式自造的，所以看起来就是前缀直接放在动词前。

abstract.en: Picture two hands pressing the same door from opposite sides with equal force.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手从两侧用同样的力推同一扇门。

abstract.en: Picture a fire and a stream of water meeting at the same point.
abstract.cn: 想象火与一股水在同一点相遇。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour and a correction walking toward each other in a narrow street.
abstract.cn: 想象谣言与更正从一条窄街的两头走向对方。

examples.en: Exercise can counteract the effects of a sedentary job.
examples.cn: 运动可以抵消久坐工作带来的影响。

examples.en: The antidote counteracts the poison within minutes.
examples.cn: 解毒剂在几分钟内就中和了毒性。

examples.en: Higher interest rates were meant to counteract rising prices.
examples.cn: 提高利率原本是为了抑制物价上涨。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「康特」加「阿克特」——两个动作迎头对撞，正好互相消掉：抵消、反制

root: 拉丁语「相反」与「行动」两词进入英语后，由英语按拉丁模式自行拼合成「反向行动」，十五世纪起见于记载。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all push back: a force, a drug, an economy, a policy's damage, an influence, a physical vector, a plan and a decaying material.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在往回推：力量、药物、经济、政策造成的损害、影响、物理矢量、计划与正在劣化的材料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two equal forces pressing the same door from opposite sides, so that it does not move at all.
core.cn: 核心意象：两股等大的力从相反方向推同一扇门，门纹丝不动。

branches.en: THE FORCE: an effect weakened by action, and a physical vector balanced by its opposite.
branches.cn: 力：被行动削弱的效应，以及被反向矢量平衡的物理力。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE: a drug cancelling another drug, and a coating slowing decay.
branches.cn: 物质：一种药抵消另一种药，涂层减缓劣化。

branches.en: THE ECONOMY AND POLICY: inflation fought by rates, damage answered by measures.
branches.cn: 经济与政策：以利率对抗通胀，以措施回应损害。

branches.en: THE INFLUENCE: rival propaganda offered against propaganda.
branches.cn: 影响：用对立宣传对抗宣传。

branches.en: THE PLAN: an intention prevented by an opposing move.
branches.cn: 计划：意图被对方的行动阻止。

intro.en: Counteract is an English compound of a Latin prefix and an English verb of Latin origin; its family is small and technical.
intro.cn: 本词是拉丁前缀与源自拉丁语的英语动词构成的英语复合词，词族较小且偏技术。

latinIntro.en: Latin contra and the participle of the verb for acting supply both pieces; Latin did not itself form this compound as a single verb.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示相反的词与表示行动的动词分词提供两个构件；拉丁语本身并未把它合成一个单词动词。

items.example: It marks the direction of the action.
items.exampleCN: 它标记行动的方向。

items.example: The Latin word behind the English prefix.
items.exampleCN: 英语前缀背后的拉丁词。

items.example: The verb supplies what is being done against something.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供被反向施行的动作。

items.example: The Latin verb behind the English one.
items.exampleCN: 英语动词背后的拉丁动词。

items.example: The participle is the shape English received.
items.exampleCN: 英语接收的是这个分词形式。

items.example: It builds the noun for the opposing act.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示反向动作的名词。

items.example: It builds the adjective for what can oppose an effect.
items.exampleCN: 它构成描述可对抗效应之物的形容词。

items.example: It builds the name of an opposing agent.
items.exampleCN: 它构成对抗性介质的名称。

items.example: It marks an effect that has already been reduced.
items.exampleCN: 它标记已被削弱的效果。

definition_en: to reach a conclusion by reasoning from evidence or from general principles
core_image: 一串脚印从泥地延伸到矮墙下，看的人顺着痕迹一步步把结论领出来
scene: 侦探看到窗台上的灰被擦去一半，便由这条痕迹推出有人从窗子进出。From the half-wiped dust the detective deduced that someone had used the window.
sceneCN: 这里指依据现场痕迹推出事实（第 6 个义项：由实物线索推断出事实）；句意：侦探从被擦去一半的灰尘推断有人用过那扇窗。

senses.title: To reach a conclusion by reasoning
senses.definition: to work out a conclusion from evidence rather than from direct observation
senses.definitionCN: 由证据而非直接观察得出一个结论
senses.example: From the marks on the wall they deduced that the water had once been higher.
senses.exampleCN: 他们从墙上的痕迹推断出水位曾经更高。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to lead down, so the mind is led from the evidence down to the conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为向下引领，心智被从证据一路领到结论。

senses.title: To derive a case from premises (logic)
senses.titleCN: 在逻辑上由前提出发推出
senses.definition: in logic, to derive a particular statement from general premises by a valid step
senses.definitionCN: 在逻辑中，由一般前提出发经有效步骤推出具体陈述
senses.example: From the two premises the class deduced that no exception could exist.
senses.exampleCN: 由这两个前提，全班推出不可能存在例外。
senses.why: Logic made the downward leading a formal procedure with rules that fix what may follow.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学把这种向下引领变成有规则约束的正式程序，规定什么可以推出。

senses.title: To trace something to its source (formal)
senses.definition: in formal or older usage, to trace a fact or a word back to its origin
senses.definitionCN: 在正式或较早用法中，把某个事实或词语追溯到其来源
senses.example: The custom may be deduced from an older harvest rite.
senses.exampleCN: 这一习俗也许可以追溯到一种更古老的收获仪式。
senses.why: Led down also means followed back along a chain, which is how origins are recovered.
senses.whyCN: 向下引领也意味着沿链条反推，追溯来源正是这样完成的。

senses.title: To work out a meaning from context
senses.definition: to infer the sense of a word or a passage from the surrounding text
senses.definitionCN: 由上下文推断词或段落的意思
senses.example: Readers deduce the meaning of an unfamiliar word from the sentence around it.
senses.exampleCN: 读者从周围的句子推断出生词的意思。
senses.why: Language gives partial evidence, and the mind fills the rest by the same leading-down path.
senses.whyCN: 语言提供部分证据，心智沿同一条向下引领的路径把其余部分补上。

senses.title: To derive a rule from data
senses.definition: to extract a general rule or pattern from a set of observations
senses.definitionCN: 从一组观察中抽出一条一般规律或模式
senses.example: The analysts deduced a seasonal pattern from three years of sales.
senses.exampleCN: 分析师从三年的销售数据推出一个季节性规律。
senses.why: Data is the premise and the rule is the conclusion, so the verb names the path between them.
senses.whyCN: 数据是前提，规律是结论，这个动词命名的是两者之间的路径。

senses.title: To infer facts from physical clues
senses.definition: to reconstruct what happened from traces left in the physical world
senses.definitionCN: 根据物质世界留下的痕迹重建事情经过
senses.example: From the half-wiped dust the detective deduced that someone had used the window.
senses.exampleCN: 侦探从被擦去一半的灰尘推断有人用过那扇窗。
senses.why: Clues are premises written in matter, and the detective's work is the old verb in its most dramatic form.
senses.whyCN: 线索是用物质写成的前提，侦探的工作就是这个古老动词最戏剧化的形态。

senses.title: To derive a formula or result (mathematics)
senses.definition: in mathematics, to obtain a result by a sequence of valid steps
senses.definitionCN: 在数学中，通过一系列有效步骤得到结果
senses.example: The students deduced the area formula from the rectangle.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们由矩形面积推出了那个面积公式。
senses.why: Mathematics is the home of the downward step, where each line must follow from the one before.
senses.whyCN: 数学是这种向下推步的主场，每一行都必须由前一行推出。

senses.title: To work out consequences of a theory
senses.definition: to set out what must follow if a theory or an assumption is accepted
senses.definitionCN: 说明若接受某个理论或假设，必然会出现什么
senses.example: If the model is right, we can deduce where the particles should appear.
senses.exampleCN: 如果模型正确，我们就能推知粒子应当出现在哪里。
senses.why: A theory is judged by its consequences, and drawing them out is the everyday work of the verb.
senses.whyCN: 理论靠其后果受检验，把后果推出来正是这个动词的日常工作。

intro.en: Deduce comes from a Latin verb meaning to lead down or to draw off, built from a prefix of downward movement and the verb for leading. English took it in the sixteenth century, and logic fixed the sense of deriving a conclusion.
intro.cn: 本词出自一个表示向下引领或引出的拉丁动词，由表示向下的前缀与表示引领的动词构成。英语在十六世纪借入，逻辑学固定了「推出结论」的含义。

items.en: Ducere meant to lead or to draw, and it stands behind many English words of conducting and producing.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为引领、牵引，英语中许多表示引导与产出的词都出自它。

items.en: The prefix meant down or away, so the compound pictured a movement downward along a path.
items.cn: 这个前缀表示向下或离开，因此复合词描绘的是沿路径向下的移动。

items.en: The Latin verb meant to lead down or to draw off, and also to derive one thing from another.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为向下引领或引出，也指由一事物导出另一事物。

items.en: Medieval logic fixed the word for the step from general premises to a particular conclusion.
items.cn: 中世纪逻辑学把这个词固定为从一般前提走向具体结论的那一步。

items.en: English borrowed it in the sixteenth century, when logic and rhetoric were school subjects.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入，当时逻辑与修辞是学校科目。

items.en: Detection, mathematics and language teaching each gave the old step a new kind of premise.
items.cn: 侦查、数学与语言教学各自给这古老的一步配上新种类的前提。

note.en: The first group shares the leading root or its English forms; the second group names nearby kinds of reasoning and seeing. Deduce moves along a chain from premises to a conclusion, while discern grasps something faint or hidden by looking closely, so a chain of steps and an act of perception must be kept apart.
note.cn: 第一组共享引领词根或其英语形式；第二组是相邻的推理与察看。本词沿前提链一步步走向结论，辨察类词则靠细看抓住模糊或隐蔽之物，推理链与感知动作必须分开。

entries.definition: The conclusion drawn, and also the sum taken away from a total.
entries.definitionCN: 推出的结论，也指从总额中扣除的数额。

entries.definition: Of reasoning that starts from general rules, the opposite of inductive.
entries.definitionCN: 指从一般规则出发的推理，与归纳相对。

entries.definition: Able to be worked out from what is given.
entries.definitionCN: 可由已知条件推出的。

entries.definition: To subtract an amount; the money sense split off from the reasoning sense.
entries.definitionCN: 减去一笔数额；金额义从推理义分出来。

entries.definition: To reach a conclusion from evidence; it does not require a formal chain of steps.
entries.definitionCN: 由证据得出结论；不要求正式的步骤链。

entries.definition: To arrive at a final judgement; it names the end, not the path.
entries.definitionCN: 得出最终判断；指终点，而非路径。

entries.definition: To obtain something from a source, often a formula or a word.
entries.definitionCN: 从某个来源得到某物，常指公式或词语。

entries.definition: To think logically in general; it may move in either direction.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指合乎逻辑地思考；可向任一方向进行。

entries.definition: To find an answer by thinking; the plain everyday phrase behind the formal verb.
entries.definitionCN: 靠思考找出答案；是正式动词背后平实的日常说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the leading root, the real family and the prepositions that mark the premise.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用引领词根、真实同族词，以及标记前提的介词。

normal.en: The root means to lead, so the verb is to be led from evidence down to a conclusion.
normal.cn: 词根意为引领，动词就是由证据被领到结论。

normal.en: The family runs deduction, deductive, deducible and the money verb deduct.
normal.cn: 同族词有推论、演绎的、可推断的，以及表示扣除的同根动词。

normal.en: The preposition is from: one deduces something from something else.
normal.cn: 介词用「由」：由某物推出另一物。

normal.en: Logic makes the step formal, and mathematics makes it visible line by line.
normal.cn: 逻辑使这步正式化，数学使它在每一行上可见。

normal.en: The detective sense is the most vivid: clues as premises written in matter.
normal.cn: 侦探义最生动：线索是用物质写成的前提。

abstract.en: Picture a path of stepping stones that only appears one stone at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一条踏脚石小路，每次只浮现一块石头。

abstract.en: Picture a locked box whose key is the shape of the lid, not a separate object.
abstract.cn: 想象一只锁箱，钥匙的形状就藏在盖子上，而不是另一件东西。

abstract.en: Picture a rope ladder let down rung by rung, each rung held by the one above.
abstract.cn: 想象一架绳梯逐级放下，每一级都由上面一级吊住。

examples.en: From the silence in the room she deduced that the news was bad.
examples.cn: 从屋里的沉默，她推断消息不好。

examples.en: We can deduce the age of the rock from the fossils in it.
examples.cn: 我们可以从岩石中的化石推断其年代。

examples.en: The rule can be deduced from a handful of examples.
examples.cn: 这条规律可以从少数几个例子推出。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「得」加「丢斯」——顺着脚印一级级往下领，最后领出结论：推断

root: 拉丁语「向下」前缀加「引领」动词构成「向下引出、导出」，中世纪逻辑学固定为「演绎推出」，十六世纪进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all lead from something given to something concluded: evidence, premises, an origin, a context, data, clues, axioms and a theory's consequences.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都是从已给之物走向结论：证据、前提、来源、语境、数据、线索、公理与理论的后果。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a line of footprints running to a low wall while a watcher follows them step by step to the conclusion.
core.cn: 核心意象：一串脚印从泥地延伸到矮墙下，看的人顺着痕迹一步步把结论领出来。

branches.en: THE CLUES: reasoning from evidence, and reconstructing an event from physical traces.
branches.cn: 线索：由证据推理，以及由实物痕迹重建事件。

branches.en: THE FORMAL CHAIN: a conclusion drawn from premises, and the consequences of a theory.
branches.cn: 形式链：由前提推出结论，以及理论的必然后果。

branches.en: THE ORIGIN: a custom or a word traced back along a chain.
branches.cn: 来源：沿着链条反推的习俗或词语。

branches.en: THE CONTEXT: a meaning recovered from the surrounding words.
branches.cn: 语境：由周围词语复原出的含义。

branches.en: THE RULE AND THE FORMULA: a pattern drawn from data and a result derived in mathematics.
branches.cn: 规律与公式：由数据抽出的模式，以及数学中导出的结果。

intro.en: Deduce is a Latin verb of leading down, and its family supplies the noun of the conclusion, the adjective of the method and a separate verb for subtraction.
intro.cn: 本词是一个表示向下引领的拉丁动词，其词族提供表示结论的名词、描述方法的形容词，以及一个表示扣除的独立动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere and the prefix de- form the verb; the English endings were added later.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示引领的动词与表示向下的前缀构成这个动词，英语词尾是后加的。

items.example: It gives the movement its downward direction.
items.exampleCN: 它给这个移动以向下的方向。

items.example: The root supplies the pulling of the mind along.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供心智被一路牵引之意。

items.example: The verb is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: English shortened the Latin verb to its modern shape.
items.exampleCN: 英语把拉丁动词缩短为现代形式。

items.example: It builds the noun for the conclusion and for subtraction.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示结论与扣除的名词。

items.example: It builds the adjective for the method of reasoning.
items.exampleCN: 它构成描述推理方法的形容词。

items.example: It builds the adjective for what can be worked out.
items.exampleCN: 它构成描述可被推出的形容词。

items.example: It builds the noun for the statements one starts from.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示出发时所依据的陈述的名词。

items.example: It builds the verb for drawing a final judgement together.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示把判断收拢起来的动词。

derivatives.zh: 同根平行动词，义为「扣除、减除」，并非由本词派生
同根平行动词，义为「归纳、引起」，并非由本词派生
由同根平行动词构成，义为「归纳的」，并非由本词派生

definition_zh: 辨明；看出；识别（细微差别）
definition_en: to see or understand something that is faint, hidden or not immediately obvious
core_image: 雾里一盏灯的轮廓慢慢从灰白中浮出来，眼睛要先分开背景才看得见它
scene: 天还没亮，守望的人从雾里辨认出远处灯塔的轮廓。In the fog the lookout discerned the outline of the lighthouse.
sceneCN: 这里指从模糊的背景中看出某物的轮廓（第 1 个义项：看清隐约或部分被遮住的东西）；句意：守望的人在雾中辨认出灯塔的轮廓。

senses.title: To perceive something faint or partly hidden
senses.titleCN: 看清隐约或被遮住之物
senses.definition: to make out an object or a sign that is dim, distant or partly concealed
senses.definitionCN: 辨认出模糊、遥远或部分被遮蔽的物体或迹象
senses.example: In the fog the lookout discerned the outline of the lighthouse.
senses.exampleCN: 守望的人在雾中辨认出灯塔的轮廓。
senses.why: The root means to sift, so seeing here is separating an object from the background that hides it.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为筛分，因此这里的看见是把物体从遮蔽它的背景中分开。

senses.title: To tell two similar things apart
senses.definition: to recognize the difference between things that look or sound alike
senses.definitionCN: 认出看起来或听起来相像之物间的差别
senses.example: A trained ear can discern the two instruments in the recording.
senses.exampleCN: 受过训练的耳朵能听出录音中的两件乐器。
senses.why: Sifting is choosing between pieces, and choosing between similar things is the same gesture applied to perception.
senses.whyCN: 筛分就是在碎片之间挑选，在相似之物间作选择是同一动作用在感知上。

senses.title: To judge wisely and see the truth
senses.definition: to understand a situation correctly, especially where others are misled
senses.definitionCN: 正确理解某种处境，尤其在旁人被误导之时
senses.example: She discerned the real reason behind the polite refusal.
senses.exampleCN: 她看出了那道客气拒绝背后的真正原因。
senses.why: Clear sight is used of the mind as well as the eye, so judgement becomes a kind of seeing.
senses.whyCN: 清晰的目光既用于眼睛，也用于心智，因此判断成为一种看见。

senses.title: To notice a pattern or trend
senses.definition: to detect a regularity that is not obvious from a single case
senses.definitionCN: 从单个事例中看不出、但能被察觉的规律性
senses.example: Analysts discern a slow shift in consumer habits.
senses.exampleCN: 分析人士看出一股消费者习惯上的缓慢变化。
senses.why: A pattern is hidden in the mass of details, and the verb names the act of separating it out.
senses.whyCN: 模式藏在大量细节里，这个动词命名的是把它分离出来的动作。

senses.title: To read someone's motives
senses.definition: to perceive what a person really intends beneath what is said
senses.definitionCN: 在所说出的话之下察觉某人真正的意图
senses.example: He could discern a little envy in her congratulations.
senses.exampleCN: 他能从她的祝贺中察觉出一点嫉妒。
senses.why: Human motives are faint signals, which is exactly what this verb is built to pick out.
senses.whyCN: 人的动机是微弱的信号，这正是这个动词生来要捕捉的东西。

senses.title: To tell right from wrong
senses.definition: to distinguish morally good conduct from bad without confusing the two
senses.definitionCN: 分清道德上的善与恶，不把两者混淆
senses.example: The old stories teach children to discern right from wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 这些古老的故事教孩子明辨是非。
senses.why: Moral judgement is described as seeing clearly, since the failure involved is a failure to distinguish.
senses.whyCN: 道德判断被描述成看得清楚，因为这里的失误就是分辨不清。

senses.title: To distinguish slight sensory differences
senses.definition: to notice small differences in taste, smell, colour or texture
senses.definitionCN: 察觉味道、气味、颜色或质地上的细微差异
senses.example: Few tasters can discern the difference between the two teas.
senses.exampleCN: 很少有品茶者能辨出这两种茶的差别。
senses.why: The senses are the original training ground for sifting, and fine tasting is its most literal survival.
senses.whyCN: 感官本是筛分能力最初的训练场，精细品鉴是它最字面的留存。

senses.title: To find structure in data or noise
senses.titleCN: 从数据或噪声中找出结构
senses.definition: to detect a real signal inside a mass of random or confusing information
senses.definitionCN: 在一大堆随机或混乱的信息中察觉真实的信号
senses.example: The software discerns a weak signal beneath the noise.
senses.exampleCN: 这套软件在噪声之下辨出一个微弱信号。
senses.why: Modern research is a new field for an old act: separating a signal from everything that covers it.
senses.whyCN: 现代研究给古老动作提供了新场地：把信号从覆盖它的一切中分离出来。

intro.en: Discern comes from a Latin verb meaning to separate and so to distinguish, built from a prefix of separation and a verb for sifting. English took it through French in the fourteenth century, and its noun became the ordinary word for judgement.
intro.cn: 本词出自一个表示分开、因而表示辨别的拉丁动词，由表示分离的前缀与表示筛分的动词构成。英语在十四世纪经法语借入，其名词后来成为表示判断力的常用词。

items.en: Cernere meant to sift or to separate, and from that came the sense of distinguishing one thing from another.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为筛分、分开，由此产生把一物与另一物区别开来的含义。

items.en: The prefix meant apart, so the compound pictured taking one thing out of a mixture.
items.cn: 这个前缀表示分开，因此复合词描绘的是把某物从混合物中取出来。

items.en: The Latin verb meant to separate, to distinguish and to perceive clearly.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为分开、区别、看清。

items.en: Old French carried the verb to English in the fourteenth century, where it settled in both sight and judgement.
items.cn: 古法语在十四世纪把这个动词带到英语，它在视觉与判断两方面都站稳了脚。

items.en: The English noun became the fixed word for good judgement, especially in moral and practical matters.
items.cn: 英语名词成为表示良好判断力的固定说法，尤其用于道德与实际事务。

items.en: Statistics and signal processing gave the old act of sifting a new object: structure hidden in noise.
items.cn: 统计学与信号处理给古老的筛分动作配上新对象：藏在噪声里的结构。

note.en: The first group shares the sifting root or its English descendants; the second group names nearby acts of seeing and distinguishing. Discern is an act of perception that separates something faint from its background, while deduce is a chain of steps from premises to a conclusion.
note.cn: 第一组共享筛分词根或其英语后裔；第二组是相邻的看见与区分动作。本词是从背景中分离出模糊之物的感知动作，推演类词则是从前提走向结论的步骤链。

entries.definition: The capacity for fine judgement, especially about people and values.
entries.definitionCN: 精细判断的能力，尤其关于人与价值。

entries.definition: Showing good judgement, as in a discerning reader.
entries.definitionCN: 显示良好判断力的，如有眼力的读者。

entries.definition: Careful about what one says; it comes from the same Latin participle but lost the seeing.
entries.definitionCN: 说话谨慎；出自同一个拉丁分词，却丢掉了「看见」之义。

entries.definition: Separate and distinct, which is the literal sense of the shared participle.
entries.definitionCN: 分开而独立的，正是那个共享分词的字面义。

entries.definition: To become aware of something through the senses; it is the general word.
entries.definitionCN: 通过感官觉察某物；是泛称。

entries.definition: To mark a difference between things; the emphasis is on the difference, not the faintness.
entries.definitionCN: 标出事物间的差别；强调差别，而非微弱。

entries.definition: To discover something hidden or hard to notice, often by instrument.
entries.definitionCN: 发现隐藏或难以察觉之物，常借助仪器。

entries.definition: To draw fine distinctions; also used for unfair treatment, a sense this word avoids.
entries.definitionCN: 作精细区分；也用于不公平对待，而本词避开后一义。

entries.definition: To manage to see or hear something with difficulty; the everyday phrase for the first sense.
entries.definitionCN: 费力地看清或听清；是第一个义项的日常说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the sifting root, the real family and the fixed phrases of perception and judgement.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用筛分词根、真实同族词，以及感知与判断方面的固定搭配。

normal.en: The root means to sift, so the verb means to separate one thing from everything around it.
normal.cn: 词根意为筛分，动词就是把某物从周围一切中分出来。

normal.en: The family runs discernment, discerning, discernible and indiscernible.
normal.cn: 同族词有辨别力、有眼力的、可辨认的与难以辨认的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: discern a difference, discern the truth, barely discern.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：辨出差别、辨明真相、勉强辨认。

normal.en: The eye and the mind share the verb, which is why judgement is described as clear sight.
normal.cn: 眼睛与心智共用这个动词，因此判断被描述成清晰的看见。

normal.en: Two look-alike adjectives came from the same participle: one means tactful, one means separate.
normal.cn: 两个形近形容词出自同一分词：一个表示谨慎，一个表示分离。

abstract.en: Picture a shape slowly separating itself from a grey wall of fog.
abstract.cn: 想象一个形状慢慢从灰色的雾墙中分离出来。

abstract.en: Picture two nearly identical threads that only a careful hand can tell apart.
abstract.cn: 想象两根几乎一样的线，只有细心的手能分开。

abstract.en: Picture a single clear note heard under the noise of a whole street.
abstract.cn: 想象整条街的喧闹下，一个清亮的音符被听见。

examples.en: It was hard to discern anything in the dark room.
examples.cn: 在漆黑的房间里很难看清任何东西。

examples.en: She discerned a note of worry beneath his calm voice.
examples.cn: 她从他平静的声音里辨出一丝担忧。

examples.en: The study discerns no clear trend in the data.
examples.cn: 这项研究在数据中看不出明确的趋势。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迪」加「森」——从雾里把轮廓一丝丝筛出来：辨明、看出

root: 拉丁语「分开」前缀加「筛分」动词构成「分开以看清」，十四世纪经法语进入英语；核心是把微弱之物从背景中筛出来。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all separate a faint thing from its background: an outline, a difference, the truth, a pattern, a motive, right from wrong, a taste and a signal in noise.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把微弱之物从背景中分离出来：轮廓、差别、真相、模式、动机、是非、味道与噪声中的信号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the outline of a lamp slowly emerging from grey fog, after the eye has separated it from the background.
core.cn: 核心意象：雾里一盏灯的轮廓慢慢从灰白中浮出来，眼睛要先分开背景才看得见它。

branches.en: THE SENSES: a dim outline made out, and two similar things told apart.
branches.cn: 感官：看清模糊轮廓，并分辨两个相似之物。

branches.en: THE JUDGEMENT: the real cause understood, and right separated from wrong.
branches.cn: 判断：理解真正原因，并把是非分开。

branches.en: THE PATTERN: a regularity extracted from a mass of detail.
branches.cn: 模式：从大量细节中抽出的规律。

branches.en: THE PERSON: an intention read beneath what is said.
branches.cn: 人：从言语之下读出的意图。

branches.en: THE FINE DIFFERENCE: a slight taste distinguished, and a weak signal found in noise.
branches.cn: 细微差别：辨出细微味道，以及在噪声中找到微弱信号。

intro.en: Discern is a Latin verb of sifting, and its family supplies the noun for judgement, two adjectives and a pair of look-alike forms that lost the visual sense.
intro.cn: 本词是一个表示筛分的拉丁动词，其词族提供表示判断力的名词、两个形容词，以及一对失去视觉义却字形相近的形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin cernere and the prefix of separation form the verb; French passed it to English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示筛分的动词与表示分离的前缀构成这个动词，法语再把它传给英语。

items.example: It marks taking one thing out of a mixture.
items.exampleCN: 它标记把某物从混合物中取出。

items.example: The root supplies the act of separating.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供分离的动作。

items.example: The verb is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: English kept a shortened form of the Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: 英语保留了拉丁动词的缩短形式。

items.example: It builds the noun for the capacity of judgement.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示判断能力的名词。

items.example: It builds both the participle and the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它既构成分词，也构成形容词。

items.example: It builds the adjective for what can be made out.
items.exampleCN: 它构成描述可被辨认之物的形容词。

items.example: It builds the adjective for what cannot be made out.
items.exampleCN: 它构成描述无法辨认之物的形容词。

items.example: It builds an adverb of manner from the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把形容词变成方式副词。

latinEntries.meaning: to sift, to separate, to perceive

definition_zh: 扭曲；使变形；歪曲（事实、意思）；使失真
definition_en: to twist something out of its true shape, or to report it in a way that no longer matches it
core_image: 一张平展的铁皮被钳子拧成螺旋，原本笔直的边成了弯的
scene: 编辑把受访者的两段话剪接在一起，前后颠倒之后，意思完全变了。The editor distorted the interview by joining two separate answers.
sceneCN: 这里指把原话剪接成与本人意思不符的样子（第 2 个义项：歪曲事实或他人的陈述）；句意：编辑把两段互不相干的回答拼在一起，歪曲了这次访谈。

senses.title: To twist something out of shape
senses.definition: to bend or twist an object so that its natural form is lost
senses.definitionCN: 弯折或拧转物体，使其失去原有形状
senses.example: The heat distorted the plastic casing.
senses.exampleCN: 高温使塑料外壳变形。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to twist apart, so the first sense is the hand's work on a solid object.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为拧开，因此第一个义项是手在固体上做的事。

senses.title: To misrepresent facts or a statement
senses.definition: to report something so that it no longer corresponds to what was said or done
senses.definitionCN: 报道某事时使其不再符合原话或原事
senses.example: The editor distorted the interview by joining two separate answers.
senses.exampleCN: 编辑把两段互不相干的回答拼在一起，歪曲了这次访谈。
senses.why: A report can be bent just as a sheet of metal can, and the same verb covers both.
senses.whyCN: 叙述像铁皮一样可以被弯折，同一个动词两边都管。

senses.title: To alter a signal so it is unfaithful
senses.definition: to change a sound, an image or a waveform so that the copy no longer matches the original
senses.definitionCN: 改变声音、图像或波形，使副本不再与原物相符
senses.example: A cheap amplifier distorts the signal at high volume.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价的放大器在高音量下会使信号失真。
senses.why: Electronics took the physical twist into the invisible: a wave's shape is bent out of truth.
senses.whyCN: 电子学把物理扭曲带进看不见的领域：波形的形状被拧离真实。

senses.title: To bias or skew statistics
senses.definition: to shape the collection or the presentation of data so that a result is pushed one way
senses.definitionCN: 在数据收集或呈现上做手脚，使结果偏向一方
senses.example: Choosing only surviving firms distorts the average.
senses.exampleCN: 只挑选存活下来的公司会使平均值失真。
senses.why: A number can be bent by the way it is gathered, so the verb moves from metal to method.
senses.whyCN: 数字能被采集方式拧弯，于是这个动词从金属转到方法。

senses.title: To distort prices or a market
senses.definition: to change prices or incentives so that they no longer reflect real costs or demand
senses.definitionCN: 改变价格或激励，使其不再反映真实成本或需求
senses.example: Subsidies distort the price of fuel across the region.
senses.exampleCN: 补贴扭曲了整个地区的燃料价格。
senses.why: Economics speaks of distorted signals when the market's information is bent by intervention.
senses.whyCN: 经济学把被干预拧弯的市场信息称为失真的信号。

senses.title: To twist the meaning of words
senses.definition: to give a word or a phrase a sense it does not properly carry
senses.definitionCN: 给一个词或短语安上它本不具备的意思
senses.example: The slogan distorts the meaning of the original promise.
senses.exampleCN: 这句口号把原来承诺的意思拧歪了。
senses.why: Meaning has a shape too, and stretching it until it fits another purpose is the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 意义也有形状，把它拉到另一用途上，用的还是同一个动词。

senses.title: Of metal or plastic under stress
senses.definition: of a material, to change shape permanently under heat or load
senses.definitionCN: 材料在高温或载荷下发生永久形变
senses.example: The beam distorted under the weight of the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 横梁在屋顶的重量下变形了。
senses.why: Engineering keeps the most literal sense and measures how far a part may bend before it fails.
senses.whyCN: 工程学保留最字面的义项，并测量构件在失效前能弯多少。

senses.title: To warp a person's public image
senses.titleCN: 把某人的公众形象写得失真
senses.definition: to present a person's character or motives in a way that exaggerates or invents
senses.definitionCN: 以夸大或编造的方式呈现某人的性格或动机
senses.example: The article distorted her as a careless manager.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇文章把她写成一个粗心的管理者，与实情不符。
senses.why: When the object is a person, the twist becomes a story that others will believe.
senses.whyCN: 当对象是一个人，这种拧转就变成一则别人会相信的故事。

intro.en: Distort comes from a Latin verb meaning to twist apart, built from a prefix of reversal and the verb for twisting. English took it in the sixteenth century, and its sense spread from bodies to reports and signals.
intro.cn: 本词出自一个表示拧开的拉丁动词，由表示反向的前缀与表示拧转的动词构成。英语在十六世纪借入，含义从物体扩展到叙述与信号。

items.en: Torquere meant to twist, and it also stands behind the words for torque and for torture.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为拧、扭，英语中表示转矩与酷刑的词也出自它。

items.en: The prefix meant apart or in different directions, so the compound pictured a twist that pulls a shape open.
items.cn: 这个前缀表示分开或朝不同方向，因此复合词描绘把形状拧开的力量。

items.en: The Latin verb meant to twist awry, and it could describe limbs, metal and speech.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为拧歪，可用于肢体、金属与言辞。

items.en: English borrowed it in the sixteenth century, first for bodies and faces, then for accounts.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入，先用于身体与面孔，再用于叙述。

items.en: Sound engineering and economics later applied the word to waves and to prices.
items.cn: 声学工程与经济学后来把这个词用到波形与价格上。

note.en: The first group shares the twisting root or its English forms; the second group names nearby ways of falsifying. Distort twists a shape or a story out of truth, whereas contaminate mixes something foreign into a clean substance, so bending and adulterating are different acts.
note.cn: 第一组共享拧转词根或其英语形式；第二组是相邻的造假方式。本词把形状或叙述拧离真实，污染类词则把外来物混进洁净之物，弯折与掺混是两种动作。

entries.definition: The bent shape, the false report or the unfaithful signal.
entries.definitionCN: 被弯的形状、失实的报道或失真的信号。

entries.definition: Already twisted out of the true form.
entries.definitionCN: 已经被拧离真实形态的。

entries.definition: The turning force that twists an object; it shares the root but is a technical noun.
entries.definitionCN: 使物体扭转的力矩；共享词根，但是技术名词。

entries.definition: A wrong for which the law gives a remedy, literally something twisted.
entries.definitionCN: 法律给予救济的侵害行为，字面意为被拧歪之事。

entries.definition: To turn something around itself; it can be literal or figurative but names no falsehood.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物绕自身转；可字面可比喻，但不含虚假之意。

entries.definition: To bend out of shape, especially by heat or damp; it stresses material change.
entries.definitionCN: 使变形，尤指受热或受潮；强调材料变化。

entries.definition: To give a false account; the emphasis is on the account rather than the twist.
entries.definitionCN: 作失实叙述；强调叙述，而非拧转。

entries.definition: To bias a result or a view; it is statistics-friendly and less physical.
entries.definitionCN: 使结果或看法偏斜；多用于统计，物理意味较弱。

entries.definition: To make false, often deliberately, as in falsifying records.
entries.definitionCN: 使变假，常指故意，如伪造记录。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the twisting root, the real family and the objects that show the physical and the figurative uses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用拧转词根、真实同族词，以及能显示字面与比喻用法的宾语。

normal.en: The root means to twist, so the verb is a twist that pulls a form away from its truth.
normal.cn: 词根意为拧，动词就是把形状拧离真实的动作。

normal.en: The family runs distortion, distorted, distortive and the technical distortionless.
normal.cn: 同族词有失真、扭曲的、造成扭曲的，以及技术用语无失真的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: distort the facts, distort the meaning, distort prices.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：歪曲事实、歪曲含义、扭曲价格。

normal.en: Electronics gives the invisible version: a wave bent away from its true shape.
normal.cn: 电子学给出看不见的版本：波形被拧离本形。

normal.en: The look-alike nouns for torque and for a legal wrong share the same twisting root.
normal.cn: 表示转矩与法律侵害的形近名词共享同一个拧转词根。

abstract.en: Picture a straight ruler held at both ends and slowly bent into an arc.
abstract.cn: 想象一把直尺两端被握住，慢慢弯成弧形。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour that grows a new detail each time it is retold.
abstract.cn: 想象一则传言每被转述一次就多出一个细节。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow stretched sideways until it no longer resembles the body.
abstract.cn: 想象影子被横向拉长，直到不再像原来的身体。

examples.en: The lens distorted the straight lines near the edge of the photo.
examples.cn: 镜头使照片边缘附近的直线变形。

examples.en: Both sides accused the other of distorting the record.
examples.cn: 双方都指责对方歪曲记录。

examples.en: A small sample can distort the overall picture.
examples.cn: 样本过小会使整体情况失真。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「迪」加「斯托特」——把铁皮拧成麻花，形状和意思都走样：扭曲、歪曲

root: 拉丁语「分开」前缀加「拧转」动词构成「拧歪」，十六世纪进入英语；从身体与面孔扩展到叙述、信号与价格。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all bend a form away from its truth: an object, a report, a signal, a statistic, a price, a word, a loaded beam and a public image.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把某种形态拧离真实：物体、报道、信号、统计、价格、词语、受载的梁与公众形象。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a flat sheet of metal gripped by pliers and twisted into a spiral, its straight edge now curved.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张平展的铁皮被钳子拧成螺旋，原本笔直的边成了弯的。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL: an object twisted by heat, and a beam bent under load.
branches.cn: 材料：被高温拧变形的物体，以及受载弯曲的梁。

branches.en: THE ACCOUNT: facts misreported, and a person's image warped into a story.
branches.cn: 叙述：被失实报道的事实，以及被写成故事的公众形象。

branches.en: THE SIGNAL: a wave or image that no longer matches the original.
branches.cn: 信号：不再与原物相符的波形或图像。

branches.en: THE NUMBER AND THE PRICE: statistics pushed one way and market signals bent by intervention.
branches.cn: 数字与价格：被推向一方的统计，以及被干预拧弯的市场信号。

branches.en: THE WORD: a meaning stretched until it serves another purpose.
branches.cn: 词语：被拉到另一用途上的意义。

intro.en: Distort is a Latin verb of twisting, and its family supplies the noun of the bent shape and the adjective of what has been bent.
intro.cn: 本词是一个表示拧转的拉丁动词，其词族提供表示被弯形状的名词，以及描述已被弯折之物的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin torquere and the prefix of reversal form the verb; the noun came into English through the Latin noun of the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示拧转的动词与表示反向的前缀构成这个动词；名词则经同一词干的拉丁名词进入英语。

items.example: It turns the twist into a twist away from the true form.
items.exampleCN: 它把拧转变成拧离本形。

items.example: The root supplies the physical act.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供这个物理动作。

items.example: The verb is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: English kept a shortened form of the Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: 英语保留了拉丁动词的缩短形式。

items.example: It builds the noun for the bent shape or the false report.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示被弯形状或失实报道的名词。

items.example: It marks the object after the twist.
items.exampleCN: 它标记被拧过之后的对象。

items.example: It builds the rare adjective for what causes distortion.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示造成扭曲的罕见形容词。

items.example: It builds the technical adjective for a faithful signal.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示信号不失真的技术形容词。

items.example: The same root survived as a mechanical noun.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根作为机械名词留存下来。

definition_en: to surround something, or to include it as part of a larger whole
core_image: 一道圆墙从四面合拢，把散落的房屋、井与树全部圈进墙内
scene: 课程说明列出的主题从基础语法一直排到学术写作，几乎没有遗漏。The course encompasses grammar, reading and academic writing.
sceneCN: 这里指课程把多个主题全部纳入范围（第 3 个义项：涵盖某一学科或主题范围）；句意：这门课程涵盖语法、阅读与学术写作。

senses.title: To surround on all sides
senses.definition: to encircle a place or an object so that it is enclosed on every side
senses.definitionCN: 把某个地方或物体从四面包起来，使其被围在中间
senses.example: High walls encompass the old courtyard.
senses.exampleCN: 高墙把这座旧庭院四面围住。
senses.why: The word begins with a picture of walking a full circle around something, which is physical enclosure.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初描绘的是绕某物走满一圈，也就是物理上的围合。

senses.title: To include as parts of a whole
senses.titleCN: 作为整体的一部分包含
senses.definition: to have a number of things inside a larger group or system
senses.definitionCN: 在一个更大的群体或系统内部容纳若干事物
senses.example: The collection encompasses works from three centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这批藏品包含三个世纪的作品。
senses.why: Once a circle is drawn, everything inside it is included, so enclosure becomes inclusion.
senses.whyCN: 圆圈一旦画定，圈内的一切便都被纳入，围合由此变成包含。

senses.title: To cover a subject or field
senses.definition: of a course, a book or a survey, to deal with a whole field of material
senses.definitionCN: 指课程、书籍或综述处理整片材料领域
senses.example: The course encompasses grammar, reading and academic writing.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课程涵盖语法、阅读与学术写作。
senses.why: A syllabus is a boundary, and whatever falls inside its line is what the course covers.
senses.whyCN: 教学大纲就是一条边界，落在界线之内的一切就是课程涵盖的内容。

senses.title: To contain the members of a category
senses.definition: in logic, of a class or a term, to have certain members within its scope
senses.definitionCN: 在逻辑中，指某个类别或术语把某些成员纳入其范围
senses.example: The category encompasses both birds and bats.
senses.exampleCN: 这个类别既包括鸟类，也包括蝙蝠。
senses.why: A category is a circle in logic diagrams, and what it encompasses is what lies inside the circle.
senses.whyCN: 在逻辑图里类别就是一个圆，它所包含的就是圆内的东西。

senses.title: To enclose a piece of land
senses.definition: of a fence, a wall or a boundary, to shut in a piece of land
senses.definitionCN: 指篱笆、围墙或边界把一片土地围起来
senses.example: The new park encompasses the old orchard and the pond.
senses.exampleCN: 新公园把旧果园与池塘都圈了进去。
senses.why: Land is the most literal object of the verb, since a boundary drawn on the ground can be walked.
senses.whyCN: 土地是这个动词最字面的宾语，因为画在地上的界线可以真的走一圈。

senses.title: Of a policy that embraces goals
senses.definition: of a plan or a policy, to take in several aims or values as one programme
senses.definitionCN: 指计划或政策把若干目标或价值纳入同一套方案
senses.example: The reform encompasses both housing and transport.
senses.exampleCN: 这项改革把住房与交通都纳入其中。
senses.why: A policy, like a wall, draws a line around what it will deal with, and that line is its scope.
senses.whyCN: 政策像围墙一样，为它要处理的事画出界线，这条界线就是它的范围。

senses.title: To go around something (old sense)
senses.definition: in older usage, to travel all the way around a place
senses.definitionCN: 在较早用法中，指绕某地走完一整圈
senses.example: The old text describes a pilgrim who encompassed the shrine.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇旧文描述一位绕行圣殿一周的朝圣者。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the walk itself, before the word became a matter of scope.
senses.whyCN: 最早的义项就是走这一圈本身，后来这个词才转向范围问题。

senses.title: To cover every case or possibility
senses.definition: to take in all relevant cases so that none is left outside
senses.definitionCN: 把所有相关情形都纳入，不留下任何一个在外面
senses.example: The rules are written to encompass every likely dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 这些规则的写法要涵盖所有可能出现的纠纷。
senses.why: Completeness is a circle with no gap in it, which is why the word can mean covering everything.
senses.whyCN: 完整就是一个没有缺口的圆，因此这个词可以表示涵盖一切。

intro.en: Encompass is an English verb built from a prefix meaning in and a noun for a circuit or a circle. The noun came from Latin by way of French, and the verb has meant both to surround and to include since the fourteenth century.
intro.cn: 本词是英语动词，由表示「进入」的前缀与表示一周、一圈的名词构成。那个名词经法语来自拉丁语，这个动词自十四世纪起就兼指环绕与包含。

items.en: Passus meant a step, and it stands behind English words for pace and for the measured stride.
items.cn: 这个拉丁名词指一步，英语中表示步幅与步测的词都出自它。

items.en: The verb meant to measure out by steps, and so to go around a space with a measured stride.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为用步子量出，因此指以等长的步幅绕一片空间走一圈。

items.en: Old French took the word for a circuit, a circle and the instrument that draws one.
items.cn: 古法语用这个词指一周、一圈，也指画圆的器具。

items.en: English borrowed the noun as a circuit or a boundary, and kept the tool sense for the magnetic compass.
items.cn: 英语借入这个名词，指一周或一条边界，并保留了指磁性罗盘的工具义。

items.en: The verb, recorded from the fourteenth century, first meant to go around and then to shut in.
items.cn: 这个动词自十四世纪有记载，先指绕行，后指围在里面。

items.en: Modern usage made inclusion the dominant sense, so a course or a policy encompasses its material.
items.cn: 现代用法让「包含」成为主导义，因此课程或政策会把其内容涵盖在内。

note.en: The first group shares the circuit noun or looks close to it; the second group names nearby kinds of inclusion and enclosure. Encompass stresses that everything lies inside one boundary, while include only says that something is among the parts.
note.cn: 第一组共享表示一圈的名词或字形相近；第二组是相邻的包含与围合类型。本词强调一切都在同一条界线之内，包含类词只说某物在组成部分之中。

entries.definition: A circuit, a range, or the instrument for drawing circles and finding direction.
entries.definitionCN: 一周、一个范围，或画圆与指示方向的器具。

entries.definition: The state of being shut in or taken in; a rare nominal form.
entries.definitionCN: 被围住或被纳入的状态；罕见的名称形式。

entries.definition: A single step, from the same root as the measured stride.
entries.definitionCN: 一步，与量步同出一个词根。

entries.definition: To go by or through, from the same root for a step.
entries.definitionCN: 经过或通过，出自同一个表示一步的词根。

entries.definition: To have something as a part; it is the plain word and implies no boundary.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物作为一部分；是平实说法，不含边界意象。

entries.definition: To consist of particular parts; it stresses the parts rather than the outline.
entries.definitionCN: 由若干部分构成；强调部分，而非外圈。

entries.definition: To deal with a subject; it is the usual word for courses and reports.
entries.definitionCN: 处理某个主题；课程与报告的常用词。

entries.definition: To hold or accept broadly, often with warmth; it adds attitude to inclusion.
entries.definitionCN: 广泛地接纳，常含热情；在包含之上加了态度。

entries.definition: To be all around something; it gives the physical picture without the scope sense.
entries.definitionCN: 在四周环抱某物；只给物理画面，不含范围义。

entries.definition: To have something inside; it can be literal or logical, but does not suggest a drawn boundary.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物装在里面；可字面可逻辑，但不含画出的界线。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the circuit noun, the real family and the phrases of courses and policies.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用表示一圈的名词、真实同族词，以及课程与政策方面的固定搭配。

normal.en: The noun inside means a circuit, so the verb is to draw that circuit around something.
normal.cn: 里面的名词意为一周，动词就是围绕某物画出这一周。

normal.en: The family runs compass, encompassment, encompassing and the rare compassable.
normal.cn: 同族词有罗盘、涵盖、涵盖广泛的，以及罕见的可围绕的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: encompass a range, encompass all aspects, be encompassed by.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：涵盖一个范围、涵盖各方面、被某物包围。

normal.en: The land sense is literal: a park that takes in an old orchard and a pond.
normal.cn: 土地义最字面：一座把旧果园与池塘圈进来的公园。

normal.en: The syllabus is a drawn line, and what falls inside it is what the course covers.
normal.cn: 教学大纲就是画出的界线，落在界内就是课程涵盖的内容。

abstract.en: Picture a rope laid on the ground in a single closed circle.
abstract.cn: 想象一根绳在地上摆成一个闭合的圆。

abstract.en: Picture a sentence that can hold every example you can think of inside its grammar.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话，它的语法装得下你能想到的所有例子。

abstract.en: Picture a net thrown over a whole orchard, branches and fruit together.
abstract.cn: 想象一张网罩住整片果园，枝与果一并罩住。

examples.en: The reserve encompasses three lakes and a stretch of forest.
examples.cn: 保护区包含三个湖泊和一片森林。

examples.en: Her report encompasses both the causes and the remedies.
examples.cn: 她的报告既涵盖原因，也涵盖补救办法。

examples.en: The old walls encompass the entire village.
examples.cn: 旧城墙把整个村庄围在里面。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「恩」加「康帕斯」——拿圆规在地上画一整圈，把东西全圈进来：包含、包围

root: 拉丁语「步」衍生出「用步子量一圈」的动词，经古法语指一周、一圈及画圆之器，十四世纪进入英语；由环绕转指包含。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one circle: physical enclosure, inclusion in a whole, a field covered, a category's members, a walled piece of land, a policy's aims, an old walk around and completeness.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着同一个圆：物理围合、作为整体的一部分、被涵盖的领域、类别的成员、圈起的土地、政策的目标、古义的绕行与完整无缺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a round wall closing from every side, taking in the scattered houses, the well and the trees.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道圆墙从四面合拢，把散落的房屋、井与树全部圈进墙内。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL RING: a place surrounded, and a park walled around an orchard and a pond.
branches.cn: 物理圆环：被围住的地方，以及把果园与池塘圈进墙内的公园。

branches.en: THE MEMBERS: works inside a collection, and members inside a logical category.
branches.cn: 成员：藏品中的作品，以及逻辑类别中的成员。

branches.en: THE SCOPE: a course covering a field, and a policy taking in several aims.
branches.cn: 范围：涵盖某一领域的课程，以及纳入多项目标的政策。

branches.en: THE OLD WALK: a pilgrim travelling all the way around a shrine.
branches.cn: 古义的绕行：朝圣者绕圣殿走完一整圈。

branches.en: THE COMPLETE CIRCLE: every case taken in, with no gap left in the line.
branches.cn: 完整之圆：所有情形都被纳入，界线没有缺口。

intro.en: Encompass is an English verb built on a noun that Latin gave to French and French to English; its family supplies the tool, the range and the rare nominal forms.
intro.cn: 本词是英语动词，其基础名词由拉丁语传给法语、再传给英语；词族提供工具、范围与罕见的名称形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin passus and the verb for measuring by steps supply the core; English added the in-prefix and the verb shape.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示一步的词与表示用步子量测的动词提供核心，英语加上表示进入的前缀与动词外形。

items.example: It puts the object inside the drawn circle.
items.exampleCN: 它把宾语放进画好的圆内。

items.example: The root supplies the measured stride.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供量步的动作。

items.example: The verb supplies the walking of a full circuit.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词提供走满一圈的动作。

items.meaning: a circuit; a circle; the tool
items.example: French passed the noun to English.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个名词传给英语。

items.example: The noun survives in the modern range sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词以现代范围义留存下来。

items.example: It builds the rare noun for the state of inclusion.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示被纳入状态的罕见名词。

items.example: It builds the participle and the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它构成分词与形容词。

items.example: It marks what has already been enclosed.
items.exampleCN: 它标记已被围入之物。

items.example: It builds the rare adjective for what can be surrounded.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示可被围绕的罕见形容词。

latinEntries.meaning: to measure out by steps, to go around

derivatives.zh: 同根基础名词，义为「罗盘、范围、圆规」，并非由本词派生
同根远亲词，义为「一步、步速」

definition_zh: 加剧；使恶化；激化（病情、问题、情绪）
definition_en: to make a bad situation, an illness or a feeling more severe
core_image: 原本只剩一点火星的炭堆被风一吹，火舌立刻窜高，把旁边的干草也点着
scene: 医生提醒病人，熬夜和饮酒会让本来稳定的病情明显加重。Late nights and alcohol exacerbate the patient's condition.
sceneCN: 这里指让病情变得更严重（第 2 个义项：使疾病或症状加重）；句意：熬夜和饮酒会加重这位病人的病情。

senses.title: To make a problem worse
senses.definition: to increase the seriousness of a difficulty that is already present
senses.definitionCN: 使已经存在的困难变得更加严重
senses.example: The new tax exacerbated the shortage of housing.
senses.exampleCN: 新税加剧了住房短缺。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to make harsher, and a problem made harsher is a problem made worse.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为使更严酷，问题变严酷就是变严重。

senses.title: To aggravate an illness
senses.definition: to make a disease, a symptom or a condition more severe
senses.definitionCN: 使疾病、症状或身体状况更加严重
senses.example: Late nights and alcohol exacerbate the patient's condition.
senses.exampleCN: 熬夜和饮酒会加重这位病人的病情。
senses.why: Medicine adopted the word because a harsh course of illness is exactly what the verb describes.
senses.whyCN: 医学采用这个词，因为病程变得凶险正是这个动词所描述的。

senses.title: To intensify a conflict
senses.definition: to make a dispute or a tension sharper and harder to settle
senses.definitionCN: 使争端或紧张局面更尖锐、更难平息
senses.example: The patrol exacerbated tensions along the border.
senses.exampleCN: 这次巡逻激化了边境的紧张局势。
senses.why: A conflict that grows sharper has taken on the bitterness the Latin adjective names.
senses.whyCN: 冲突变得更尖锐，正是染上了那个拉丁形容词所指的苦涩。

senses.title: To worsen economic conditions
senses.definition: to make an economic situation more difficult or unstable
senses.definitionCN: 使经济形势更困难或更不稳定
senses.example: A sudden rise in fuel costs exacerbated the slowdown.
senses.exampleCN: 燃料成本骤升加剧了经济放缓。
senses.why: An economy already slowing is a bad state, and the verb adds severity to something that exists.
senses.whyCN: 已经放缓的经济本就是坏状态，这个动词给已有之事再加上一层严重。

senses.title: To inflame a person's feelings
senses.definition: to make anger, grief or fear stronger and less controlled
senses.definitionCN: 使愤怒、悲伤或恐惧更强烈、更难控制
senses.example: The rumour exacerbated the crowd's anger.
senses.exampleCN: 这则传言使人群的愤怒更加激烈。
senses.why: The oldest English use was about irritated feeling, before the medical sense became dominant.
senses.whyCN: 英语中最早的用法就是被激怒的情绪，早于医学义成为主流。

senses.title: To worsen environmental damage
senses.definition: to increase the harm done to air, water, soil or living systems
senses.definitionCN: 加重对空气、水、土壤或生命系统的损害
senses.example: Draining the wetland exacerbated the loss of species.
senses.exampleCN: 排干湿地加剧了物种的消失。
senses.why: Environmental harm is an existing bad process, and any added pressure is an exacerbation of it.
senses.whyCN: 环境损害是一个已经存在的坏过程，任何外加压力都是对它的加剧。

senses.title: To make an injury or pain worse
senses.definition: to increase the severity of a wound or of physical pain
senses.definitionCN: 使伤口或身体的疼痛更加严重
senses.example: Walking on the ankle too soon exacerbated the injury.
senses.exampleCN: 脚踝过早承重使伤势加重。
senses.why: A wound is the most physical case, and the verb keeps the body in view even when the object is abstract.
senses.whyCN: 伤口是最物理的情形，即使宾语抽象，这个动词仍保留身体的画面。

senses.title: To deepen inequality or disadvantage
senses.titleCN: 加剧不平等或弱势处境
senses.definition: to make an existing gap in wealth, access or opportunity wider
senses.definitionCN: 使财富、机会或获取途径上已有的差距更大
senses.example: The fee structure exacerbated the gap between rich and poor schools.
senses.exampleCN: 这套收费结构加剧了富裕学校与贫困学校之间的差距。
senses.why: A gap is imagined as a cut in a surface, and making it deeper is the same picture as making a problem worse.
senses.whyCN: 差距被想象成表面的一道切口，把它弄得更深与把问题弄得更糟是同一幅画。

intro.en: Exacerbate comes from a Latin verb meaning to make harsher, built on an adjective for bitter and severe. English took it in the fifteenth century through French, and medicine gave it its modern prominence.
intro.cn: 本词出自一个表示使更严酷的拉丁动词，其基础是一个表示苦涩与严酷的形容词。英语在十五世纪经法语借入，医学给了它今天的显著地位。

items.en: Acer meant sharp, keen or fierce, and it stands behind words for sourness and for sharpness of temper.
items.cn: 这个拉丁形容词意为尖锐、强烈、猛烈，英语中表示酸味与脾气尖刻的词都出自它。

items.en: Acerbus meant bitter, harsh and unripe, and it described both taste and manner.
items.cn: 这个拉丁形容词意为苦涩、严酷、未成熟，既描述味道，也描述态度。

items.en: The prefix meant out or thoroughly, and here it intensified the harshness.
items.cn: 这个前缀表示向外或彻底，在这里加强了严酷的程度。

items.en: The Latin verb meant to make bitter or harsh, and to irritate or provoke.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为使苦涩、使严酷，也指激怒、刺激。

items.en: English took the verb through French in the fifteenth century, first for irritated feelings.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪经法语借入，先用于被激怒的情绪。

items.en: Nineteenth-century medicine made the verb the standard word for a disease growing worse.
items.cn: 十九世纪的医学使这个动词成为表示病情加重的标准说法。

note.en: The first group shares the bitter root or its English relatives; the second group names nearby ways of making something worse. Exacerbate always makes an existing bad thing worse, while counteract pushes back against an effect, so the two point in opposite directions.
note.cn: 第一组共享苦涩词根或其英语亲属；第二组是相邻的使坏加重的说法。本词总是让已经不好的事更糟，对抗类词则朝效应回推，两者方向相反。

entries.definition: A sharpening of a disease or of a problem.
entries.definitionCN: 疾病或问题的急剧加重。

entries.definition: Sharp and bitter in speech; it describes the manner, not the worsening.
entries.definitionCN: 言辞尖刻苦涩；描述态度，而非加重过程。

entries.definition: Bitterness in relations, which is what exacerbation often produces.
entries.definitionCN: 关系中的尖刻敌意，常是加剧之后的结果。

entries.definition: Sharp and unpleasant to smell or taste; the sensory relative of bitter.
entries.definitionCN: 刺鼻难闻的；是苦涩在感官上的亲属。

entries.definition: To become or make worse; it is the plain word without the sense of sharpening.
entries.definitionCN: 变坏或使变坏；是平实说法，不含「变尖锐」之意。

entries.definition: To make worse, especially an illness or an offence; it is close but often stronger in medicine.
entries.definitionCN: 使更严重，尤指病情或过失；意思接近，医学中常用得更重。

entries.definition: To make stronger; it need not be bad, since intensity can be neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 使更强；不一定坏，因为强度可以是中性的。

entries.definition: To stir up strong feeling or to make a body part red and sore.
entries.definitionCN: 激起强烈情绪，或使身体部位红肿疼痛。

entries.definition: To raise the degree of something; it can be neutral or positive.
entries.definitionCN: 提高某种程度；可为中性或正面。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the bitter root, the real family and the objects that show what can be made worse.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用苦涩词根、真实同族词，以及能显示可使恶化之对象的搭配。

normal.en: The root means bitter, so the verb means to make a thing more bitter than it already was.
normal.cn: 词根意为苦涩，动词就是让本来苦涩的事更加苦涩。

normal.en: The family runs exacerbation, exacerbating, exacerbated and the related adjective acerbic.
normal.cn: 同族词有加重、使恶化的、被加重的，以及同根的「尖刻」形容词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: exacerbate a problem, exacerbate symptoms, exacerbate tensions.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：使问题恶化、加重症状、激化紧张局势。

normal.en: Medicine is its strongest home: a disease that grows sharper is the standard case.
normal.cn: 医学是它最主要的归宿：病程变得凶险是标准情形。

normal.en: It never means to create a problem, only to make an existing one worse.
normal.cn: 它从不表示制造问题，只表示让已有的问题更严重。

abstract.en: Picture a small flame fanned by a sudden wind until it catches the dry grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一点小火被突来的风一吹，烧着了干草。

abstract.en: Picture a crack in a wall widened by one hard frost.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上的一道裂缝被一场严霜撑得更宽。

abstract.en: Picture an angry word that makes a whole room angrier.
abstract.cn: 想象一句愤怒的话让满屋的人更愤怒。

examples.en: Cutting the budget would exacerbate the staffing problem.
examples.cn: 削减预算会使人员问题更加严重。

examples.en: Cold air can exacerbate a lung condition.
examples.cn: 冷空气可能加重肺部疾病。

examples.en: The delay exacerbated the dispute between the two sides.
examples.cn: 这次拖延激化了双方的争端。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「伊格」加「扎瑟贝特」——往苦药里再加一把苦艾，病更难受：加剧、恶化

root: 拉丁语「尖锐」衍生出「苦涩、严酷」的形容词，加表示彻底的强意前缀构成「使更严酷」，十五世纪经法语进入英语，十九世纪在医学中定型。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all sharpen something already bad: a problem, an illness, a conflict, an economy, a feeling, the environment, an injury and an inequality.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都把已经不好的事变得更尖锐：问题、疾病、冲突、经济、情绪、环境、伤势与不平等。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heap of embers fanned by a sudden gust, flames leaping up and catching the dry grass beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：原本只剩一点火星的炭堆被风一吹，火舌立刻窜高，把旁边的干草也点着。

branches.en: THE PROBLEM: a difficulty made worse, and an economy pushed further down.
branches.cn: 问题：变得更严重的困难，以及被进一步压下去的经济。

branches.en: THE BODY: a disease aggravated and an injury made more painful.
branches.cn: 身体：被加重的疾病与被弄得更痛的伤势。

branches.en: THE CONFLICT AND THE FEELING: sharper tensions and angrier emotions.
branches.cn: 冲突与情绪：更尖锐的紧张局势与更激烈的情绪。

branches.en: THE ENVIRONMENT: harm to water, air and living systems increased.
branches.cn: 环境：对水、空气与生命系统的损害被加重。

branches.en: THE GAP: inequality between groups made wider.
branches.cn: 差距：群体之间的不平等被拉大。

intro.en: Exacerbate is a Latin verb of bitterness and severity, and its family supplies the noun of worsening and adjectives for the sharp manner behind it.
intro.cn: 本词是一个表示苦涩与严酷的拉丁动词，其词族提供表示恶化的名词，以及描述其背后尖刻态度的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin acer and acerbus supply the bitter core, and the prefix ex- supplies the intensifying push.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示尖锐与苦涩的两个形容词提供苦涩核心，前缀提供加强的推力。

items.example: It intensifies the harshness of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它加强那个形容词的严酷程度。

items.example: The root supplies the edge of the meaning.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供意义的锋刃。

items.example: The adjective supplies the taste and the manner.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供味道与态度。

items.example: The verb is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是英语词的直接来源。

items.example: It gives the Latin stem an English verb shape.
items.exampleCN: 它给拉丁词干披上英语动词外形。

items.example: It builds the medical noun for a sharp turn for the worse.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示病情急剧转坏的名词。

items.example: It builds the participle and the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它构成分词与形容词。

items.example: It marks a condition already made worse.
items.exampleCN: 它标记已经被加重的状况。

items.example: It builds the related adjective for bitter speech.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示言语尖刻的同根形容词。

definition_zh: 促进；使便利；便利（某事发生）；主持引导（讨论）
definition_en: to make an action, a process or a discussion easier to carry out
core_image: 原本堵在门口的杂物被搬开，队伍不必再侧身挤过，一步就进了门
scene: 主持人把话筒递给一直沉默的成员，让讨论得以继续。The chair facilitated the discussion by inviting the quiet members to speak.
sceneCN: 这里指主持人引导讨论、使交流顺畅进行（第 2 个义项：以主持人的身份引导讨论或会议）；句意：主持人请沉默的成员发言，使讨论得以推进。

senses.title: To make an action easier
senses.definition: to remove an obstacle so that something can be done with less effort
senses.definitionCN: 移除障碍，使某件事做起来更省力
senses.example: Better signs facilitate the flow of visitors through the museum.
senses.exampleCN: 更清楚的指示牌使参观者在馆内的流动更顺畅。
senses.why: The Latin adjective inside the word means easy, so the verb means to make easy.
senses.whyCN: 这个词里的拉丁形容词意为容易，因此动词意为使容易。

senses.title: To guide a discussion or meeting
senses.definition: to run a discussion so that participants can speak and decide without being directed
senses.definitionCN: 主持讨论，使参与者能够发言并作出决定，而不被强加方向
senses.example: The chair facilitated the discussion by inviting the quiet members to speak.
senses.exampleCN: 主持人请沉默的成员发言，使讨论得以推进。
senses.why: A chair is there to make talk possible, and the modern meeting sense is the plain literal one.
senses.whyCN: 主持人存在的意义就是让谈话成为可能，现代会议义其实就是最字面的用法。

senses.title: To create conditions for growth
senses.definition: to provide the circumstances in which a process can develop well
senses.definitionCN: 提供某种过程得以良好发展的环境条件
senses.example: Warm water and sunlight facilitate the growth of algae.
senses.exampleCN: 温暖的水与阳光促进藻类生长。
senses.why: Growth cannot be commanded, but the conditions for it can be made easy to reach.
senses.whyCN: 生长无法被命令，但生长所需的条件可以被弄得容易达到。

senses.title: To help communication between parties
senses.definition: to make it easier for two parties to exchange information or reach agreement
senses.definitionCN: 使两方更容易交换信息或达成一致
senses.example: A neutral adviser facilitated the talks between the two sides.
senses.exampleCN: 一位中立的顾问促成了双方的会谈。
senses.why: When two parties cannot hear each other, someone can remove the obstacle between them.
senses.whyCN: 当双方听不见彼此，总有人可以搬走横在中间的障碍。

senses.title: Of a biological process helped along
senses.definition: in biology, to assist a process that would otherwise be slow or blocked, as in facilitated diffusion
senses.definitionCN: 在生物学中，指帮助原本缓慢或受阻的过程，如易化扩散
senses.example: The channel proteins facilitate the movement of ions across the membrane.
senses.exampleCN: 通道蛋白促进离子跨膜移动。
senses.why: Cells have helpers that lower the barrier for a molecule, which is the same picture on a tiny scale.
senses.whyCN: 细胞有帮忙者，为分子降低门槛，这是同一幅画在极小尺度上的版本。

senses.title: To ease the spread of something
senses.definition: to make the spread of information, goods or a problem easier, often without endorsing it
senses.definitionCN: 使信息、货物或某个问题更容易扩散，通常并不表示赞成
senses.example: Fast networks facilitate the spread of both news and falsehood.
senses.exampleCN: 高速网络既便利新闻传播，也便利虚假信息传播。
senses.why: The verb is neutral about what spreads: it only reports that the path is easier.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词对扩散内容保持中立，只报告路径变容易了。

senses.title: To provide access
senses.definition: to make something reachable by removing practical barriers
senses.definitionCN: 移除实际障碍，使某物更容易获得
senses.example: The ramp facilitates access to the building for wheelchair users.
senses.exampleCN: 坡道使轮椅使用者更容易进入这栋建筑。
senses.why: Access is an obstacle course, and anything that removes a step is facilitating it.
senses.whyCN: 获取本身就是一道障碍赛，任何减少一步的东西都在促进它。

senses.title: To make learning easier
senses.definition: in teaching, to arrange material and tasks so that learners can progress with less friction
senses.definitionCN: 在教学中，安排材料与任务，使学习者遇到的阻力更小
senses.example: Clear examples facilitate learning more than long explanations.
senses.exampleCN: 清楚的例子比长篇解释更能促进学习。
senses.why: Teaching is largely the art of removing obstacles, which is why this verb appears in every method book.
senses.whyCN: 教学很大程度上就是移除障碍的手艺，因此这个动词出现在每一本教学法著作里。

intro.en: Facilitate comes from a Latin adjective meaning easy, which itself came from the verb for doing or making. French turned it into a verb, and English borrowed it in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: 本词出自一个意为容易的拉丁形容词，那个形容词又来自表示做、造的动词。法语把它变成动词，英语在十六世纪借入。

items.en: Facere meant to do or to make, and it stands behind a very large English family of verbs and nouns.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为做、造，英语中一大群动词与名词都出自它。

items.en: Facilis meant easy to do, and it also described a person who is easy to deal with.
items.cn: 这个拉丁形容词意为容易做，也形容一个人好相处。

items.en: French made a verb from the adjective, meaning to make easy or to help along.
items.cn: 法语由这个形容词造出动词，意为使容易、予以便利。

items.en: English borrowed the verb in the sixteenth century, first for making a task less difficult.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入，先用于使任务不那么困难。

items.en: Modern management and education gave it the specialized sense of guiding a discussion or a class.
items.cn: 现代管理与教育给了它引导讨论或课堂的专门含义。

note.en: The first group shares the easy root or its English family; the second group names nearby kinds of helping. Facilitate removes an obstacle, while counteract cancels an effect, so helping and opposing are separate acts.
note.cn: 第一组共享「容易」词根或其英语词族；第二组是相邻的帮忙方式。本词移除障碍，对抗类词取消效应，帮忙与对抗是两种不同的动作。

entries.definition: The act of making something easier or of guiding a group.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事更容易或引导一个群体的动作。

entries.definition: The person who removes obstacles or guides a discussion.
entries.definitionCN: 移除障碍或引导讨论的人。

entries.definition: A building or a service, and also ease in doing something.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑或服务设施，也指做事的便利。

entries.definition: Too easy, and therefore shallow; the negative side of the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 过于容易因而浅薄；同一词根的负面一面。

entries.definition: To congratulate; it looks close but comes from a word for happiness.
entries.definitionCN: 祝贺；字形相近，却出自表示幸福的词。

entries.definition: To make less painful or less difficult; it is the plain verb behind the formal one.
entries.definitionCN: 使少些痛苦或少些困难；是正式词背后的平实动词。

entries.definition: To make something possible; possibility is the point, not effort.
entries.definitionCN: 使成为可能；重点在可能性，而非费力程度。

entries.definition: To help a person or a process; it may add direct effort.
entries.definitionCN: 帮助一个人或一个过程；可能加入直接的努力。

entries.definition: To speed something up; it is about time rather than ease.
entries.definitionCN: 加快某事；关注时间，而非省力。

entries.definition: To encourage growth or acceptance; it carries a positive attitude that this word lacks.
entries.definitionCN: 鼓励增长或接受；带有本词所缺的正面态度。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the easy root, the real family and the objects that show what is being made easier.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用「容易」词根、真实同族词，以及能显示被便利之事的宾语。

normal.en: The adjective inside means easy, so the verb means to make easy.
normal.cn: 里面的形容词意为容易，动词就是使容易。

normal.en: The family runs facilitation, facilitator, facility and the adjective facile.
normal.cn: 同族词有促进、引导者、设施，以及形容词轻易的。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: facilitate communication, facilitate access, facilitate learning.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：促进沟通、便利获取、促进学习。

normal.en: The meeting sense is literal: a chair exists to make talk possible.
normal.cn: 会议义最字面：主持人的存在就是让谈话成为可能。

normal.en: The verb is neutral about the content: good news and false news can both be helped along.
normal.cn: 这个动词对内容中立：好消息与假消息都能被便利传播。

abstract.en: Picture clutter moved away from a doorway so that people walk straight through.
abstract.cn: 想象堵在门口的杂物被搬开，人们径直走过。

abstract.en: Picture oil poured on a stuck hinge until the door swings freely.
abstract.cn: 想象给卡住的铰链上油，门便自由转动。

abstract.en: Picture a guide who opens one gate after another without walking the path for you.
abstract.cn: 想象一位向导打开一道道门，却不替你走路。

examples.en: The new software facilitates collaboration across teams.
examples.cn: 这款新软件促进了跨团队协作。

examples.en: She facilitated the workshop without offering her own answers.
examples.cn: 她主持了这次研讨，却不抛出自己的答案。

examples.en: Warm water facilitates the chemical reaction.
examples.cn: 温水促进了这一化学反应。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「法西里」加「泰特」——把门槛搬走，事情一步就过去了：使便利、促进

root: 拉丁语「做、造」动词衍生出「容易」的形容词，法语据此造出「使容易」的动词，十六世纪进入英语；现代管理与教育扩展为引导讨论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all remove friction: a task, a discussion, a growth condition, a negotiation, a biological process, a spread, an access route and a lesson.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在减少摩擦：任务、讨论、成长条件、谈判、生理过程、扩散、获取路径与一堂课。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: clutter pulled away from a doorway so that a queue no longer has to squeeze through sideways.
core.cn: 核心意象：原本堵在门口的杂物被搬开，队伍不必再侧身挤过，一步就进了门。

branches.en: THE PATH: a task made easier, and access opened by a ramp.
branches.cn: 路径：被弄得更容易的任务，以及用坡道打开的获取通道。

branches.en: THE TALK: a meeting guided, and communication helped between parties.
branches.cn: 谈话：被引导的会议，以及被协助的双方沟通。

branches.en: THE PROCESS: conditions arranged for growth, and a biological step helped along.
branches.cn: 过程：为成长安排的条件，以及被帮助的生理步骤。

branches.en: THE SPREAD: news, goods or falsehood moving faster through an easier channel.
branches.cn: 扩散：新闻、货物或虚假信息沿更顺畅的通道移动得更快。

branches.en: THE LESSON: material arranged so that learning meets less resistance.
branches.cn: 课堂：把材料安排好，使学习遇到的阻力更小。

intro.en: Facilitate is a Latin adjective turned into a verb by French, and its family supplies the process, the person and the ambiguous noun for ease or a building.
intro.cn: 本词是由法语把一个拉丁形容词变成动词的产物，其词族提供过程、人，以及兼指便利与建筑的歧义名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere and facilis supply the core, and French added the verb-forming ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示做与容易的两个词提供核心，法语加上动词词尾。

items.example: The root supplies the act of making.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供「造」这个动作。

items.example: The adjective supplies the whole meaning of ease.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供全部的「容易」含义。

items.example: French added the verb shape English borrowed.
items.exampleCN: 法语加上英语所借入的动词外形。

items.example: It fits the borrowed stem into English conjugation.
items.exampleCN: 它把借来的词干纳入英语变位。

items.example: It builds the name of the process.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示过程的名称。

items.example: It builds the name of the person who guides.
items.exampleCN: 它构成引导者的名称。

items.example: It builds the adjective for what promotes a process.
items.exampleCN: 它构成描述促进过程之物的形容词。

items.example: It builds the noun for ease, which also names buildings.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示便利的名词，也指建筑。

items.example: It builds the adjective with the negative sense of too easy.
items.exampleCN: 它构成带「过于容易」负面义的形容词。

definition_zh: 制定；构想；明确表述；按配方配制
definition_en: to express an idea precisely, or to work out a plan, rule or product in a fixed form
core_image: 散在纸上的几条意见被写进一张带编号的配方单，每一行都有确定的分量与顺序
scene: 团队把几周的讨论写成一份可执行的方案，交给上级审批。The team formulated a plan that could be carried out step by step.
sceneCN: 这里指把想法写成一份具体的行动方案（第 3 个义项：制定计划、政策或策略）；句意：团队制定了一份可以逐步执行的计划。

senses.title: To express an idea precisely
senses.definition: to state an idea in clear, exact words so that it can be examined
senses.definitionCN: 用清楚准确的语言说出一个想法，使其可被检验
senses.example: He formulated the problem in one short sentence.
senses.exampleCN: 他用一句短话把问题精确表述出来。
senses.why: A formula is a fixed form, and to formulate is to put thought into such a form.
senses.whyCN: 配方或公式是一种固定格式，而制定表述就是把思想放进这种格式。

senses.title: To write a formula in symbols
senses.definition: in chemistry or mathematics, to write a relation or a compound in standard symbols
senses.definitionCN: 在化学或数学中，用标准符号写出一个关系或一种化合物
senses.example: The students formulated the equation for the reaction.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们写出了这个反应的方程式。
senses.why: Symbols are the most exact kind of fixed form, so the word fits mathematics most literally.
senses.whyCN: 符号是最精确的固定格式，因此这个词在数学里最为字面。

senses.title: To devise a plan or policy
senses.definition: to work out a course of action in a form that others can follow
senses.definitionCN: 把一套行动安排成别人可以照着做的形式
senses.example: The team formulated a plan that could be carried out step by step.
senses.exampleCN: 团队制定了一份可以逐步执行的计划。
senses.why: A plan must be given a shape before it can be shared, and giving it shape is the work of this verb.
senses.whyCN: 计划必须先有形状才能被共享，而给它形状正是这个动词的工作。

senses.title: To state a theory precisely
senses.definition: to put a hypothesis into a form that can be tested and criticized
senses.definitionCN: 把假说放进一种可以被检验与批评的形式
senses.example: Newton formulated laws that still describe ordinary motion.
senses.exampleCN: 牛顿提出了至今仍能描述日常运动的定律。
senses.why: A theory that stays vague cannot be tested, so formulating it is the first condition of science.
senses.whyCN: 含糊的理论无法检验，因此把它精确表述是科学的第一条件。

senses.title: To prepare a product to a formula
senses.definition: to mix a medicine, a food or a material according to a fixed recipe
senses.definitionCN: 按照固定配方混合药物、食品或材料
senses.example: The lab formulated the cream for sensitive skin.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室为敏感肌肤配出了这款乳霜。
senses.why: Here the formula is a recipe rather than an equation, and the verb means to make the mixture.
senses.whyCN: 这里的配方是食谱而不是方程，动词意为把混合物做出来。

senses.title: To frame a question or argument
senses.titleCN: 把问题或论证组织成形
senses.definition: to arrange a question or an argument so that its parts are clear and ordered
senses.definitionCN: 把问题或论证安排得部分清楚、次序分明
senses.example: A good interviewer formulates the next question from the answer just given.
senses.exampleCN: 好的采访者会根据刚得到的回答组织下一个问题。
senses.why: Thinking becomes visible when it is given an order, and the verb names that ordering.
senses.whyCN: 思想在被赋予次序时才变得可见，这个动词命名的是那个安排次序的动作。

senses.title: To draw up rules or regulations
senses.definition: to set out rules in an official and precise wording
senses.definitionCN: 用正式而精确的措辞写出规则
senses.example: The committee formulated the rules for the new grant.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会拟订了这项新资助的规则。
senses.why: Rules must be fixed in words before they can bind anyone, which is a formal version of formulation.
senses.whyCN: 规则必须先固定成文字才能约束人，这是「成形」的正式版本。

senses.title: To compose a response or statement
senses.definition: to prepare a reply or a public statement in careful wording
senses.definitionCN: 用审慎的措辞准备一份答复或公开声明
senses.example: The office formulated a short response to the complaint.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构对投诉拟定了一份简短回应。
senses.why: A response is an idea that must be given a public shape before it leaves the room.
senses.whyCN: 回应是一个必须先在室内成形、才能送出房间的想法。

intro.en: Formulate comes from the Latin noun for a small mould or a fixed pattern, and from a verb meaning to shape it. French passed the verb to English in the eighteenth century, and its senses spread from recipes to policies.
intro.cn: 本词出自拉丁语中表示小模子或固定格式的名词，以及一个意为按此成形的动词。法语在十八世纪把这个动词传给英语，含义从配方扩展到政策。

items.en: Forma meant shape, mould or pattern, and it stands behind the whole English family of form words.
items.cn: 这个拉丁名词指形状、模子或格式，英语中一整族与形式有关的词都出自它。

items.en: Formula was a small mould, and then a fixed wording or a set pattern.
items.cn: 这个拉丁名词原指小模子，后来指固定的措辞或既定的格式。

items.en: The verb meant to shape something or to set it down in a fixed form.
items.cn: 这个拉丁动词意为使成形，或按固定格式写下。

items.en: French carried the verb forward in the sense of putting an idea into exact words.
items.cn: 法语把这个动词推进到「把想法放进确切措辞」的意义。

items.en: English took it in the eighteenth century, when scientific and legal writing needed exact statements.
items.cn: 英语在十八世纪借入，当时科学与法律写作都需要精确陈述。

items.en: Chemistry kept the recipe sense, while policy and management took the planning sense.
items.cn: 化学保留了配方义，政策与管理则取用了制定计划之义。

note.en: The first group shares the shape root or its English family; the second group names nearby kinds of putting ideas into form. Formulate stresses giving an idea a precise and workable shape, while facilitate stresses removing obstacles so that work can proceed.
note.cn: 第一组共享形状词根或其英语词族；第二组是相邻的「使想法成形」方式。本词强调给想法一个精确可用的形状，便利类词强调搬走障碍让工作得以前进。

entries.definition: A fixed set of symbols, a recipe or a worn phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 一组固定的符号、一份配方或一句套话。

entries.definition: The wording produced, and the act of producing it.
entries.definitionCN: 产生的措辞，以及产生它的动作。

entries.definition: Made to a fixed pattern, often in a negative sense of stale wording.
entries.definitionCN: 按固定格式做成，常含措辞陈旧之贬义。

entries.definition: The arrangement of a page or a file, from the same shape root.
entries.definitionCN: 页面或文件的排列方式，出自同一形状词根。

entries.definition: To invent or work out a plan; the emphasis is on invention, not exact wording.
entries.definitionCN: 发明或想出计划；强调发明，而非精确措辞。

entries.definition: To put a question or a statement into words; it stresses the frame around it.
entries.definitionCN: 把问题或陈述组织成话；强调外围框架。

entries.definition: To write a first version; it need not be precise yet.
entries.definitionCN: 写出初稿；此时还不必精确。

entries.definition: To express clearly in speech; it stresses clear delivery rather than planned form.
entries.definitionCN: 口头清楚表达；强调表达清楚，而非计划好的形式。

entries.definition: To put parts together into a whole, as in writing or music.
entries.definitionCN: 把各部分组合成整体，如写作或音乐。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the shape root, the real family and the objects that show planning, science and recipes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用形状词根、真实同族词，以及能显示计划、科学与配方的宾语。

normal.en: The root means shape, and a small mould is inside the noun, so the verb means to give an idea a mould.
normal.cn: 词根意为形状，名词里含有一个小模子，因此动词意为给想法一个模子。

normal.en: The family runs formula, formulation, formulaic and formulator.
normal.cn: 同族词有公式、表述、公式化的与制定者。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: formulate a plan, formulate a policy, formulate a theory.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：制定计划、制定政策、提出理论。

normal.en: Chemistry keeps the literal recipe sense, and politics keeps the planning sense.
normal.cn: 化学保留字面的配方义，政治保留制定计划的义项。

normal.en: A statement that cannot be put into exact words has not yet been formulated.
normal.cn: 还不能被放进确切措辞的陈述，就还没有被制定成形。

abstract.en: Picture loose notes on a table being copied into numbered lines of a recipe card.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上散乱的笔记被抄进一张带编号的配方卡。

abstract.en: Picture a shapeless lump of clay pressed into a mould and coming out with edges.
abstract.cn: 想象一团没有形状的黏土被压进模子，出来时有了棱角。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd of opinions reduced to one sentence everyone can read.
abstract.cn: 想象一堆意见被归结为每个人都能读到的一句话。

examples.en: The committee formulated a set of rules for the competition.
examples.cn: 委员会为这项比赛制定了一套规则。

examples.en: She formulated her objection in two precise sentences.
examples.cn: 她用两句精确的话表述了自己的反对意见。

examples.en: The company formulated a new fuel from plant waste.
examples.cn: 这家公司用植物废料配制出一种新燃料。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛」加「缪」加「莱特」——把散乱的想法压进一个模子，出来就有棱有角：制定、表述

root: 拉丁语「形状、模子」衍生出「小模子、固定格式」，再加动词词尾构成「使成形」，经法语于十八世纪进入英语；由配方扩展到政策与理论。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all give an idea a fixed shape: exact words, symbols, a plan, a theory, a recipe, a question, a rule and a public reply.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都给想法一个固定形状：准确措辞、符号、计划、理论、配方、问题、规则与公开答复。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: loose notes on a table copied into a numbered recipe card, every line with a fixed amount and a fixed order.
core.cn: 核心意象：散在纸上的几条意见被写进一张带编号的配方单，每一行都有确定的分量与顺序。

branches.en: THE STATEMENT: an idea put into exact words, and a question or an argument ordered.
branches.cn: 陈述：被放进准确措辞的想法，以及被安排好次序的问题或论证。

branches.en: THE SYMBOLS AND THE THEORY: an equation written, and a hypothesis made testable.
branches.cn: 符号与理论：写出的方程，以及变得可检验的假说。

branches.en: THE PLAN: a course of action shaped so that others can follow it.
branches.cn: 计划：成形后别人可以照着走的行动安排。

branches.en: THE RECIPE: a medicine, food or material mixed to a fixed formula.
branches.cn: 配方：按固定配方混合的药物、食品或材料。

branches.en: THE OFFICIAL WORD: rules drawn up, and a reply carefully worded.
branches.cn: 正式文字：拟订的规则与措辞审慎的答复。

intro.en: Formulate is a Latin noun of shape turned into a verb, and its family supplies the formula, the wording and the adjective for stale patterns.
intro.cn: 本词是由一个表示形状的拉丁名词变成的动词，其词族提供公式、措辞，以及描述陈旧格式的形容词。

latinIntro.en: Latin forma and formula supply the core, and the verb ending was added first in Latin and then carried by French.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示形状与小模子的两个名词提供核心，动词词尾先在拉丁语加上，再由法语带过来。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of a fixed outline.
items.exampleCN: 词根提供固定轮廓的观念。

items.meaning: a small mould; a fixed wording
items.example: The noun is the direct base of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是英语词的直接基础。

items.meaning: to shape, to set in a form
items.example: The Latin verb supplies the action.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词提供动作。

items.example: French carried the verb into English.
items.exampleCN: 法语把这个动词带进英语。

items.example: It gives the borrowed stem its English shape.
items.exampleCN: 它给借来的词干披上英语外形。

items.example: It builds the noun for the wording produced.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示所产生措辞的名词。

items.example: It builds the adjective for fixed, stale patterns.
items.exampleCN: 它构成描述固定陈旧格式的形容词。

items.example: It builds the name of the person who draws up the formula.
items.exampleCN: 它构成拟订者之名。

items.example: The shortest descendant of the same root.
items.exampleCN: 同一词根最短的后裔。

latinEntries.meaning: a small mould; a fixed form of words
